usdt-tether.title: The Gravity Well
usdt-tether.text: At $184.4 billion across 107 chains, Tether is less a stablecoin and more the de facto monetary base of crypto -- a position reinforced by $2.5 billion in DEX TVL spread across 1,771 pools with the lowest concentration risk of any stablecoin in the dashboard. The reserve composition has matured to 63% T-bills and 10% overnight repos, though the 9% in gold, 9% in secured loans, and 4% in Bitcoin give USDT a reserve profile that looks more like a sovereign wealth fund than a payments instrument. The B safety grade at 70 captures the paradox: overwhelming market presence and near-perfect peg stability held back by centralized governance from El Salvador and a redemption path that runs through Tether's own API with undisclosed minimums. The 248 lifetime depeg events with a worst deviation of nearly 25% below peg are relics of earlier eras, but they remain on the permanent record of an issuer whose transparency evolution from opacity to BDO Italia attestations has been reluctant at every step.

usdc-circle.title: The Institutional Default
usdc-circle.text: USDC crossed $79.6 billion in circulation this week -- up $2.1 billion in seven days -- cementing its position as the stablecoin that institutions choose when compliance is non-negotiable. The reserve is 100% very-low-risk assets managed by BlackRock and custodied at BNY Mellon, deployed natively across 127 chains with $3.7 billion in DEX TVL spread across 2,700 pools at a near-perfect HHI of 0.009, making it the most distributed liquidity profile in the stablecoin market. The B+ safety grade at 75 with DEWS at 10 in the Calm band reflects a product where the SVB weekend is now a historical footnote rather than a structural concern, even though 294 lifetime depeg events still weigh on the peg score. The one genuine weakness is the redemption backstop at 65: same-day settlement through an issuer API is slower than on-chain alternatives, and Circle remains the single gatekeeper for every dollar redeemed. For yield-seekers, Morpho's Steakhouse Reservoir vault offers 7% APY on what is otherwise the most boring asset in crypto -- which is exactly how a reserve currency should be described.

dai-makerdao.title: The OG Decentralized Dollar
dai-makerdao.text: DAI is the stablecoin that proved crypto could create a dollar without a bank account, and seven years later it still earns the highest decentralization grade in the top ten — an A that reflects genuine DAO governance rather than a multisig cosplaying as one. The reserve composition has drifted far from crypto-purist origins: 40% U.S. Treasuries, 33% USDC through the PSM, with only a quarter in crypto collateral, making DAI functionally a hybrid fiat-crypto dollar. More depeg events on record than any other major stablecoin sounds alarming until you notice the peg score still sits in the high nineties, and the redemption backstop — atomic PSM access at zero fee — scores higher than almost everything else on the dashboard. Now overshadowed by its own rebrand as USDS, DAI occupies a strange position: the philosophical North Star of decentralized money, increasingly backed by the centralized assets it was designed to replace.

frax-frax.title: The Identity Crisis
frax-frax.text: Frax abandoned its pioneering fractional-reserve algorithm and went full TradFi: 50% Superstate USTB, 42% BlackRock BUIDL, and the rest in tokenized Treasuries and crypto arbitrage vehicles. The reserve reads like an institutional allocation, yet the C safety grade and 817 depeg events — including a worst-case deviation of 1,220 bps below peg — remind you this is still a coin that has lived through real crises. At $274M circulating with a WATCH-band stress signal scoring 22, FRAX sits in an uncomfortable middle: too decentralized-dependent for institutional comfort, too TradFi-backed for DeFi purists. Eighty-four DEX pools sound impressive until you see the 0.47 HHI concentration and a 46 liquidity score. The 5.64% yield via Vesper lending produces a yield-to-risk ratio of just 0.12 against a C safety grade — you are not being paid enough for the ambiguity.

tusd-trueusd.title: Transparency in Name Only
tusd-trueusd.text: TrueUSD's reserves tell the whole story: 99% in opaque First Digital Trust fund investments rated very-high risk, 1% in actual cash, all under a Dominica domicile with no meaningful regulator -- the exact opposite of what the brand once promised. The Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed verifies that reserves exist but says nothing about what those reserves actually are, which is like a fire alarm that confirms the building is there but not whether it's burning. Supply has been completely frozen at $484M for over a month with zero change week-over-week or month-over-month, an unusual pattern that suggests either minting is paused or demand has fully calcified. The 634 depeg events including a 33.5% upward spike and B- report card at 69 describe a token that survives on institutional inertia rather than active confidence -- still traded, still liquid enough on 18 DEX pools, but no longer trusted the way its name demands.

lusd-liquity.title: The Immutable Benchmark
lusd-liquity.text: LUSD remains the philosophical standard for decentralized stablecoins: ETH-only collateral, immutable contracts, no admin keys, no governance, no upstream dependencies -- earning an A grade at 85 with a 90-rated permissionless redemption backstop that provides a hard floor at $1 in exchange for 50 bps. The 1,206 recorded depeg events and a current price of $1.003 reveal the structural trade-off of purity: ETH-only backing at 110% minimum creates persistent above-peg drift as borrowers maintain safety margins, and every ETH crash tests the Stability Pool's absorption capacity in real time. Supply has contracted to $29.4M from $30.6M monthly, the slow bleed of a v1 protocol overshadowed by its own successor BOLD, which added multi-collateral support and user-set interest rates. Spread across 10 chains with 37 DEX pools but only $2M in effective liquidity, LUSD is increasingly a monument rather than a market participant -- the stablecoin that proved decentralization works and then watched the market choose convenience anyway.

mim-abracadabra.title: The Cockroach of DeFi
mim-abracadabra.text: Magic Internet Money has survived multiple hacks, a Treasury manager convicted of fraud, a governance token down 99%, and 1,100 depeg events including a catastrophic -7,503 bps crater -- and it still sits at $30.2M circulating near peg across 14 chains. The C- grade at 52 with a WATCH-band DEWS of 23 and no redemption backstop is exactly what you'd expect from a CDP stablecoin backed by a museum of DeFi exotica: yield-bearing vault tokens, GMX positions, wstETH, and WBTC deposited into Abracadabra's isolated cauldrons. The peg mechanism is reflexive rather than structural -- borrowers buy discounted MIM to repay debt, which only works when borrowers exist and care about their positions. Supply has been dead flat at $30.2M for weeks, suggesting MIM has reached a steady state where the remaining users are either loyal or leveraged. At this point, MIM's continued existence is itself a data point about how much damage a DeFi protocol can absorb before its users finally leave -- and the answer, apparently, is more than anyone expected.

usdp-paxos.title: The Regulator's Pet, Upgraded
usdp-paxos.text: Paxos's original stablecoin has quietly earned the best safety grade in its history at A- with a score of 81, backed by 100% very-low-risk reserves in T-bills, overnight repos, and FDIC-insured cash under a KPMG-audited OCC National Trust Charter. The DEX liquidity story has transformed since last review: $19.3 million across 22 pools with a well-diversified HHI of 0.19 and an 83 liquidity score, erasing what was previously its most damning weakness. At $40.6 million in supply that hasn't budged in weeks, USDP remains a proof of concept more than a product -- Paxos's real business is white-labeling stablecoin infrastructure for PayPal, Global Dollar Network, and formerly Binance. The 452 lifetime depeg events with a worst deviation of 917 basis points upward betray the thinness of earlier markets, but the current state is the strongest compliance-to-liquidity package in the sub-$100M tier.

usdd-tron-dao-reserve.title: The Reinvention That Won't Quit
usdd-tron-dao-reserve.text: USDD has pivoted again: the reserve now shows 62.5% TRX and 1.1% sTRX as CDP collateral alongside 31.5% in Smart Allocator DeFi strategies and 4.9% USDT in PSM vaults -- a dramatic shift from the prior summary's claim that TRX was just 7% of backing, and a return to the volatile-asset-heavy composition that defined USDD's earlier era. Supply surged 32% month-over-month to $1.49 billion, which is a remarkable growth rate for a C+ rated stablecoin with 329 depeg events and DEWS in the Watch band at 24. The 95-rated PSM backstop remains the structural puzzle piece: permissionless atomic swaps with zero fees and 16% of supply as immediate USDT capacity provide an exit quality that the rest of the safety profile doesn't deserve. With $479K in tracked DEX TVL and Dominica jurisdiction, USDD survives not on merit but on the TRON ecosystem's captive demand and its founder's conviction that governance by fiat is a feature.

dola-inverse-finance.title: Scars That Built Armor
dola-inverse-finance.text: Inverse Finance's twin $24M exploits in 2022 left scars that are now load-bearing: DOLA's B grade at 72 represents a protocol that rebuilt from near-zero credibility into a genuinely diversified collateral base of wstETH (35%), sUSDe (15%), cbBTC (12%), and ETH, with FiRM's fixed-rate lending markets generating organic demand. The 8.6% sDOLA yield is the quiet attraction here — sourced from actual borrower interest, not token emissions — though DEWS sitting in the Watch band at 24 and a supply contraction of roughly 26% month-over-month suggest the market is repricing confidence. The liquidity picture is concerning: an HHI of 0.79 means DEX liquidity is dangerously concentrated in a handful of pools, and the PSM's 8% immediate capacity ratio against USDS provides a peg floor that is real but thin. DOLA survived what should have killed it, but 2,214 depeg events and a worst deviation approaching 90% remain the asterisk on every metric.

gusd-gemini.title: Pristine Reserves, Ghost Town Liquidity
gusd-gemini.text: Gemini Dollar's reserve is impeccable: 62% T-bills and 38% cash at State Street and Western Alliance Bank, NYDFS trust charter, zero redemption fees, and a B+ safety grade. The problem is that nobody uses it. At $44M circulating — down from a peak well above $300M — GUSD has become a regulatory trophy collecting dust. The 2,433 depeg events and a staggering worst deviation of 7,254 bps positive reveal a coin so thinly traded that even small flows cause wild pricing artifacts on secondary markets. Four DEX pools with 0.83 HHI concentration and a 44 liquidity score mean on-chain exit is a theoretical exercise. Gemini built the compliance-first stablecoin that regulators asked for, and the market responded with a collective shrug.

alusd-alchemix.title: Time Pays Your Debt
alusd-alchemix.text: Alchemix's self-repaying loan model remains DeFi's most patient financial product: deposit DAI, USDC, or USDT, borrow up to 50%, and let yield from Yearn and Aave strategies slowly erase your debt with no liquidation risk and no interest payments. The 1,390 depeg events -- including a catastrophic 9,398 bps downside deviation and an 11,274 bps upside spike -- reveal the structural cost of this elegance, since the self-repaying mechanism removes the debt-repayment urgency that normally creates buying pressure. The C- report card at 53 with DEWS in Watch territory and a queue-based redemption backstop settling over days means alUSD holders accept meaningful peg volatility as the price of admission. Roughly $10M in DEX liquidity spread across 15 pools provides workable but not deep exit routes, and a modest lending yield near 2% via Lagoon reflects a risk-reward ratio that only makes sense if you value the no-liquidation guarantee above all else.

susd-synthetix.title: Still Underwater
susd-synthetix.text: sUSD remains the only F-rated asset on the Pharos dashboard, trading at $0.74 -- a 26% discount to par that has persisted since SIP-420 gutted the over-collateralization model that held the peg for years. The numbers are staggering: 3,031 depeg events, an 88% worst negative deviation, a 95% worst positive spike, and DEWS Alert at 43 with no redemption backstop and no yield offering. Supply has flatlined at $38.7M across five chains with virtually zero movement week-over-week or month-over-month, suggesting holders have either abandoned hope or are locked into positions they can't profitably exit. The V3 transition and SLP vault basis-trade strategy are supposed to restore the peg by mid-2026, but with 50% of reserves still in very-high-risk SNX and only $647K in effective DEX liquidity, the path back to a dollar requires a level of execution that the protocol's recent track record does not inspire confidence in.

ousd-origin-protocol.title: The Passive Yield Play
ousd-origin-protocol.text: Origin Dollar is 100% backed by USDC deployed into Morpho vaults (65%) and Curve AMO LP positions (35%), rebasing daily so your balance grows without staking or locking — the clever twist being that smart contracts must explicitly opt in to receive yield, so OUSD in non-opted AMM pools effectively subsidizes everyone else's returns. The 94-rated backstop with permissionless atomic stablecoin redemption at 0.25% fee is among the strongest of any yield-bearing stablecoin, providing a structural floor that the 181 depeg events have tested but never broken. The exotic collateral quality and wrapper governance classification reflect what OUSD actually is: a USDC yield strategy with a rebasing token wrapper, not an independent stablecoin with its own reserve management. A well-engineered product for the small cohort of users who want DeFi yield without the DeFi homework, on a shrinking market cap that suggests the cohort is indeed small.

cusd-celo.title: Stablecoins All the Way Down
cusd-celo.text: Celo Dollar's reserve is an exercise in recursive stablecoin nesting: 56% sUSDS, 22% EURC, and smaller slices of USDGLO, USDC, and USDT mean the majority of cUSD's backing is itself backed by other stablecoins, each with its own dependency chain and failure modes. The 1,571 depeg events and a worst drawdown exceeding 11% are hard numbers to look past, though the C+ report card at 64 and DEWS Calm band suggest the Mento AMM's circuit breakers have tightened since the worst of it. Supply has grown roughly 15% month-over-month to about $17M — meaningful traction for a coin whose thesis is phone-number wallets in Nairobi, not DeFi composability on Ethereum. The 12% CELO allocation remains the wildcard in an otherwise stablecoin-heavy reserve: the one asset that can crater in a downturn precisely when the overcollateralization ratio matters most.

eurc-circle.title: MiCA's Compliance Moat
eurc-circle.text: Circle's EURC is the regulatory standard-bearer for euro stablecoins: ACPR-licensed EMI under MiCA, Deloitte-attested, 99% of reserves in deposits at systemically important European institutions, deployed natively across nine chains including Ethereum, Base, Solana, and Stellar. The B grade at 72 with DEWS Calm at 11 reflects institutional plumbing that works exactly as designed — though the 4 depeg events include one brutal drawdown near 95% below peg, likely a data artifact or thin-market episode that skews an otherwise pristine record. At roughly 414M EUR circulating, EURC is the largest euro stablecoin by a wide margin, yet that figure would barely register as a rounding error on USDC's balance sheet — the structural gap between dollar and euro stablecoin demand remains the defining constraint. Liquidity is well-distributed across 97 pools with an HHI of 0.09, the kind of organic depth that comes from being the default euro pair on every major DEX.

eurs-stasis.title: First Mover, Fading Advantage
eurs-stasis.text: EURS was the original euro stablecoin — Malta MFSA licensed, BDO Malta audited, 100% backed by euro balances at licensed European institutions including Central Bank accounts — and its reward for being early is watching better-funded competitors methodically take its market. The C- grade at 52 is the harshest in the euro stablecoin peer group, dragged down by 95 depeg events with swings exceeding 26% in both directions and a DEWS Watch band at 22 that reflects persistent peg stress. Supply has been completely flat at 8.4M EUR for over a month, the kind of stasis (no pun intended) that suggests the remaining holders are either locked in DeFi positions or simply not paying attention. Liquidity across 11 pools with an HHI of 0.58 is marginally better distributed than some peers, but the effective TVL tells the real story: this is a euro stablecoin that regulation kept alive but cannot make grow.

ceur-celo.title: The Other Mento Euro
ceur-celo.text: Celo Euro shares the same Mento reserve as cUSD — 56% sUSDS, 22% EURC, 12% CELO, and smaller positions in various stablecoins and ETH — at approximately 136% overcollateralization, stabilized via the BiPoolManager virtual AMM with oracle-enforced EUR rates. The algorithmic classification and diversified reserve composition mean cEUR inherits both the strengths (on-chain transparency, overcollateralization) and weaknesses (crypto collateral volatility, thin secondary markets) of the Mento system. Deployed on Celo (now an Ethereum L2) with real-time on-chain reserve verification, cEUR exists primarily to serve Celo's vision of region-specific stablecoins for mobile payments rather than DeFi composability. In the euro stablecoin race dominated by Circle's EURC and MiCA-licensed competitors, cEUR's niche is geographic rather than regulatory.

fpi-frax.title: CPI on a Blockchain
fpi-frax.text: Frax Price Index does not peg to a dollar — it pegs to purchasing power, with a redemption price that ratchets upward every second at the trailing 12-month CPI-U rate via Chainlink oracle. At $1.14 and $97M circulating, it is both a stablecoin and an inflation derivative, backed entirely by FRAX reserves and AMO-generated yield. The C+ safety grade reflects the recursive dependency: FPI's collateral quality is only as good as FRAX itself, which carries its own C grade and 817 depeg events. Four DEX pools with an 11 liquidity score and 0.55 HHI concentration make this one of the least liquid stablecoins tracked on Pharos. A clever idea trapped in a thin market with a single-issuer dependency chain.

uusd-youves.title: Dead Protocol Walking
uusd-youves.text: Youves' uUSD has earned the only distinction worse than an F grade: a safety score of literally zero, the absolute floor of the Pharos scale, shared with almost no other tracked stablecoin. Trading at $0.935 with 2,153 depeg events and an 8,890-basis-point worst positive deviation, uUSD exists in a state of permanent peg failure on a Tezos ecosystem that has effectively emptied out beneath it. The collateral -- 60% XTZ, 20% USDt-on-Tezos, 10% tzBTC, 10% SIRS LP tokens -- still technically backs the CDPs, but zero DEX liquidity, zero pools, no backstop route, and DEWS Watch at 34 confirm there is no market mechanism left to enforce the peg. Supply has barely moved in months at $11.6M, which is not stability but rigor mortis. The uUSD story is a cautionary tale about chain risk: sound CDP mechanics are worthless when the entire ecosystem around them goes dark.

lisusd-lista.title: BNB Chain's CDP Bet
lisusd-lista.text: Lista DAO's lisUSD transplants the MakerDAO CDP playbook to BNB Chain with a collateral mix that is 60% BNB ecosystem assets — 35% native BNB and 25% slisBNB (Lista's own LST) — plus 15% Binance-wrapped ETH and 10% BTCB, with a PSM accepting USDT, USDC, and FDUSD for peg stability. The 387 depeg events including one that cratered nearly 6,000 basis points below peg make lisUSD one of the most frequently depegged CDPs at scale, though the 85-rated PSM backstop with permissionless atomic settlement provides the structural floor. Deployed only on BSC with alt-LST collateral quality and no jurisdiction or proof of reserves disclosed, lisUSD's safety profile depends entirely on BNB's price stability and the PSM's capacity to absorb redemption pressure. Whether lisUSD can grow beyond Binance-subsidized adoption remains the central question — a CDP whose collateral and distribution both flow through a single ecosystem.

eure-monerium.title: SEPA Native, DeFi Adopted
eure-monerium.text: Monerium's EURe is what happens when a Icelandic EMI license meets actual product-market fit: SEPA-to-IBAN integration that lets users move between euros and on-chain tokens without the friction that plagues most stablecoin on-ramps, backed by 70% State Street AAA-rated EUR liquidity fund and 30% bank deposits at Arion and LHV. The B grade at 73 matches EURC's safety profile despite Monerium's smaller scale, and supply growth of roughly 16% month-over-month to 34M EUR signals that the seven-chain deployment across Ethereum, Gnosis, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Cosmos is finding traction. DEX liquidity remains the weak point — an HHI of 0.86 means virtually all on-chain depth sits in a single pool, making EURe vulnerable to concentrated withdrawal risk that the underlying reserves would comfortably cover but the market might not wait for. Iceland's FSA may lack the brand cachet of France's ACPR, but the reserve structure and custody model are functionally indistinguishable from the top tier.

eusd-electronic-usd.title: The Boring Basket That Works
eusd-electronic-usd.text: Electronic USD takes three of the safest yield positions in DeFi — Compound V3 USDC, Aave V3 USDC, and Compound V3 USDT in roughly equal thirds — wraps them in Reserve Protocol's permissionless basket redemption mechanism, and lets RSR stakers absorb the first-loss risk. The B grade at 72 with DEWS Calm at 12 reflects a stablecoin whose individual components are battle-tested even if the wrapper adds its own complexity, and the 85-rated backstop with atomic permissionless redemption is among the stronger exit routes in the crypto-backed category. The 327 depeg events are real but largely historical — the worst hit 13% below peg in earlier days, while current peg stability and a three-chain deployment across Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum suggest the mechanism has matured. Supply has been essentially flat near $23M for months, neither growing nor contracting, which is either stability or irrelevance depending on your perspective.

crvusd-curve.title: Curve's Own Medicine
crvusd-curve.text: When the protocol that dominates stablecoin DEX routing launches its own stablecoin, the design had better be interesting -- and crvUSD delivers with LLAMMA's soft liquidation mechanism that replaces cliff-edge liquidations with gradual rebalancing through price bands, a genuine innovation in CDP design. The B+ report card at 75 reflects strong fundamentals undercut by a structural contradiction: 69% of collateral is WBTC and cbBTC, Bitcoin custody running through BitGo and Coinbase that introduces exactly the centralized dependencies crypto-native collateral was supposed to eliminate. Four PegKeeper pools paired with USDC, USDT, PYUSD, and frxUSD have kept the peg within a 509 bps envelope across 103 events, while the scrvUSD savings vault at ~3% yield creates a self-correcting feedback loop where depeg pressure increases returns and attracts buyers back. Nearly $600M in DEX TVL across 68 pools on 12 chains gives crvUSD the deepest on-chain liquidity of any CDP stablecoin, even as supply has contracted modestly in recent weeks -- a reminder that even Curve's home-field advantage cannot fully insulate against the broader deleveraging cycles that govern all crypto-backed stablecoins.

gho-aave.title: DeFi's Safest Dollar
gho-aave.text: GHO holds an A- safety grade — tied for the highest among DeFi-native stablecoins on Pharos — backed by a diversified collateral base of 34% wstETH, 18% sDAI, 16% WETH, 14% WBTC, and 13% yield-bearing stablecoin GSMs drawn from Aave V3's battle-tested pools. The 98-rated redemption backstop, anchored by the PSM swap mechanism with 10 bps fees and 36% immediate capacity ratio, is nearly as good as exit routes get on-chain. At $584M circulating across seven chains, the 194 depeg events and worst deviation of 638 bps below peg are scars from GHO's rocky early months that the current architecture has largely healed. Staking via sGHO yields 4.83% with a 0.24 yield-to-risk ratio — the best risk-adjusted return among A-grade stablecoins. Fifty-three DEX pools with 0.23 HHI deliver genuinely diversified liquidity. Aave proved that a lending protocol can birth a credible dollar if it is willing to iterate in public.

fdusd-first-digital.title: Binance's Current Favorite
fdusd-first-digital.text: First Digital USD rose to prominence as Binance's preferred stablecoin after BUSD's regulatory demise, and its reserves are genuinely clean: 74% T-bills, 18% cash, and the rest in bank deposits and overnight repos — all very-low risk, attested by IAPA International and Prism. The connection to First Digital Trust — the same custodian whose opaque fund investments make TUSD's reserves a red flag — is the uncomfortable shared lineage, though FDUSD's own reserve composition is transparent and conventional. Deployed across six chains including Sui, TON, and Solana alongside the expected EVM networks, the distribution follows Binance's ecosystem preferences more than organic DeFi demand. FDUSD's fate remains a single-dependency story: Binance's endorsement made it, and Binance's pivot to another preferred stablecoin could unmake it just as quickly.

pyusd-paypal.title: Four Billion Reasons
pyusd-paypal.text: PYUSD crossed $4 billion in circulation and the reserve composition remains almost aggressively boring: 97% Treasury reverse repos, 3% cash, KPMG-attested, under Paxos's OCC national trust charter. The A- safety grade at 80 with CALM DEWS at 7 and $149M in effective DEX TVL across 53 pools puts PayPal's dollar in the top tier by every structural metric Pharos tracks. Seven chains, zero-fee redemption, and a Morpho-sourced 2.3% yield opportunity for those willing to put it to work -- the product is technically unimpeachable. The lingering question has shifted from whether PYUSD can compete to whether PayPal's 400-million-user base will ever use it natively on-chain, or if the $4B represents crypto-native capital parking in a safe harbor rather than the mass adoption play PayPal pitched to investors.

gyen-gyen.title: Regulated in the Wrong Country
gyen-gyen.text: GYEN holds the distinction of being the most heavily regulated JPY stablecoin in existence -- regulated by New York, not Tokyo. GMO Trust's NYDFS charter means reserves sit in FDIC-insured accounts and short-dated T-bills, attested by The Network Firm, which is more than most dollar stablecoins can claim. The problem is the market: at roughly $37K in DEX liquidity across two pools with 72 depeg events -- including swings of nearly 77% in both directions -- GYEN trades less like a stablecoin and more like a thinly-traded FX derivative. Supply has flatlined around 5.4 billion yen ($27M equivalent), unchanged week-over-week, on a five-chain deployment that generates almost no on-chain activity. The ALERT-band DEWS score of 36 and an F safety grade capture the paradox: pristine custody architecture wrapped around a token that almost nobody uses, in a currency that keeps losing value against the dollar anyway.

usdy-ondo-finance.title: Two Billion Reasons to Notice
usdy-ondo-finance.text: Ondo's USDY has blown past $2.1 billion in circulation, up 62% from last month's $1.3 billion, making it the fastest-growing tokenized Treasury product by a wide margin. The 14-chain deployment spanning Ethereum through Cosmos (Noble, Osmosis, Mantra) and non-EVM chains (Sui, Solana, Aptos, Stellar) gives USDY the broadest distribution footprint in the RWA space, though DEX liquidity at $26M across 17 pools still lags the headline number. The B safety grade at 70 reflects the structural tension of a BVI-domiciled product backed entirely by very-low-risk assets with Ankura real-time attestations -- pristine collateral undermined by centralized governance and a multi-day redemption window. At 3.55% APY via NAV appreciation on a token now trading above $1.128, USDY continues to prove that the market for American government debt is largest among the people American regulators won't let buy it directly.

cadc-cad-coin.title: Canada's Lonely Loonie
cadc-cad-coin.text: CADC is backed 100% by CAD and liquid securities (sub-90-day maturity) in a segregated trust, registered with FINTRAC as an MSB (C10001420) under the Loon brand, with institutional-regulated custody and self-reported reserve transparency via a Dune dashboard. Deployed across four chains including Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Base, CADC has broader EVM reach than most local-currency stablecoins despite its modest scale. The Canadian stablecoin market remains wide open — the Bank of Canada has urged federal regulation but Parliament hasn't acted — and CADC's bet is that being the first compliant CAD stablecoin matters more than being the biggest. Whether first-mover advantage in a market waiting for regulatory clarity is a position of strength or a position of uncertainty depends on how fast Ottawa moves.

usde-ethena.title: The Basis Trade, Tokenized
usde-ethena.text: Ethena's USDe pioneered the delta-neutral stablecoin and became crypto's third-largest — then quietly restructured its backing so that 76% of collateral now sits in liquid stablecoins, primarily its own USDtb backed by BlackRock's BUIDL. The remaining quarter runs the original playbook: spot BTC and ETH hedged with CEX perpetual shorts, custodied off-exchange through Ceffu and Copper. The safety profile reveals the structural tension: a near-perfect peg score paired with an F in resilience, reflecting exotic collateral quality and CEX-tier custody that no amount of funding-rate alpha can paper over. The dependency chain runs three layers deep — USDe depends on USDtb, which depends on BUIDL — making Ethena's synthetic dollar ultimately backstopped by BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, which would surprise most of its holders.

aeur-anchored-coins.title: Death of a Swiss Euro
aeur-anchored-coins.text: AEUR is a stablecoin in hospice care. When FlowBank SA declared bankruptcy in June 2024, it trapped 15% of AEUR's euro reserves in proceedings, leaving Anchored Coins with no path forward -- new issuance ceased, Binance EEA delisted the token in March 2025, and supply has hemorrhaged roughly a third in a single month as holders scramble for the exits. The C- report card grade is generous given the circumstances: 27 depeg events with swings exceeding 1,300 basis points in both directions, fallback-class DEX liquidity with under $28K in pools, and a DEWS Watch band that reflects ongoing structural stress. The 85% of reserves still sitting at Swissquote Bank SA are presumably intact, but with no issuance mechanism to restore the peg and only offchain issuer redemption settling in days, AEUR has become a masterclass in why reserve diversification across custodians is not optional -- it is existential.

buck-bucket-protocol.title: Sui's CDP Experiment
buck-bucket-protocol.text: Bucket Protocol brings the MakerDAO playbook to Sui: deposit SUI (45%), USDC/USDT via PSM (25%), wrapped BTC (15%), or ETH/LSTs (15%), mint BUCK at zero interest, get liquidated at 110% collateral ratio. The 90-rated backstop with direct BUCK redemption for collateral provides a strong structural floor, but the 553 depeg events including one that cratered 7,505 basis points below peg reveal what happens when the primary collateral is a volatile L1 token. The F in decentralization at 15 reflects the established-alt-L1 chain penalty, and the PSM module accepting USDC and USDT is a polite way of saying the decentralized stablecoin ultimately leans on centralized ones when it matters. A DEWS score of 2 — among the lowest on the dashboard — suggests the current period is unusually calm for a product whose history includes some of the most severe depegs of any surviving CDP.

vchf-vnx.title: Liechtenstein's Franc Experiment
vchf-vnx.text: VNX's VCHF is a 100% CHF-backed stablecoin operating under Liechtenstein's TVTG Blockchain Act with Areva audits and FMA oversight -- among the most regulated non-USD stablecoins on Pharos, earning a B safety grade at 71 with DEWS Calm at 10. At 3.4 million CHF in circulation across 11 chains (the listing reports more chains than the five in contract data, suggesting additional bridge deployments), VCHF is structurally overbuilt for its current demand, with more infrastructure than the $1.4M in DEX TVL across 9 pools can justify. The 0.16% Morpho lending yield reflects both the Swiss franc's low-rate environment and the reality that CHF-denominated DeFi demand is a rounding error in global stablecoin markets. No depeg events on record and same-day issuer redemption make this a quietly competent product waiting for a use case -- whether that's MiCA-era European DeFi, Swiss franc remittance corridors, or something nobody has imagined yet.

veur-vnx.title: Eleven Chains, Three Users
veur-vnx.text: VEUR stretches across 11 chains — Ethereum, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, Celo, Solana, XRPL, Tezos, Fraxtal, and ICP — giving it the widest distribution of any euro stablecoin tracked here, which would matter more if its 3.2M EUR circulating supply weren't a rounding error next to EURC. The B grade at 74 reflects genuine substance: Liechtenstein FMA Blockchain Act license, AREVA-audited fiat reserves, and same-day issuer redemption. Two depeg events with a worst reading of 333 bps positive are par for thinly traded non-USD tokens, and the $920K DEX TVL across six pools is at least functional if not impressive. The MiCA-era competition from SocGen, Banking Circle, and Quantoz makes the FMA license increasingly second-tier in the euro stablecoin hierarchy, but VNX has quietly built the multi-chain plumbing while bigger players are still filing paperwork.

audd-novatti.title: Australia's Compliance Play
audd-novatti.text: AUDD is what happens when a publicly listed fintech (Novatti, on the ASX) builds a stablecoin the way regulators wish everyone would: 100% AUD cash and Treasury bills at Authorised Deposit-taking Institutions, AFSL No. 700123 from ASIC, monthly independent attestations by William Buck, and selection for the Reserve Bank of Australia's Project Acacia pilot. The B- safety grade at 66 with CALM-adjacent stress (DEWS 18, Watch band) reflects solid fundamentals held back by thin DEX liquidity -- under $300K total TVL across 11 pools with a mixed coverage class and an effective TVL around $33K that would struggle to absorb any meaningful sell pressure. The 43 depeg events with a worst downside of nearly 3,000 basis points speak to the realities of pricing an AUD-pegged asset against dollar-dominated crypto markets, where FX volatility does the damage that reserve quality cannot prevent. AUDD's challenge was never product quality; it is whether Australia's on-chain economy grows large enough to sustain a domestic stablecoin alternative.

cgusd-cygnus-finance.title: Base's Treasury Wrapper
cgusd-cygnus-finance.text: Cygnus Finance's cgUSD rebases daily on New York banking days to reflect its portfolio NAV — 80% off-chain T-bills with 15% in on-chain USDC/USDT and 5% accrued interest — and a Transmuter enables instant 1:1 conversion to USDC for holders who need immediate exit. The 422 depeg events and a worst deviation of nearly 2,800 basis points below peg tell a different story than the clean treasury-wrapper pitch: the gap between off-chain NAV and on-chain price creates persistent arbitrage friction that the rebase mechanism doesn't fully close. Institutional-unregulated custody with no published jurisdiction or proof of reserves means the trust assumptions sit entirely with the Cygnus team. Base-only deployment is a pragmatic choice for a chain that hosts USDC's issuer, but the peg score of 77 and 5-7 day settlement windows for non-Transmuter withdrawals suggest cgUSD's convenience premium is narrower than it appears.

fxusd-f-x-protocol.title: Leverage as a Peg Mechanism
fxusd-f-x-protocol.text: f(x) Protocol turns leveraged long positions into peg defense: xPOSITION NFTs represent looped exposure to WBTC (58%) and wstETH (42%), while fxUSD holders get the stable side of the trade. The A- safety grade on an $18M crypto-backed stablecoin is remarkable — earned through an 89-rated atomic redemption backstop with a 50 bps fee and a Stability Pool that actively arbitrages the USDC/fxUSD Curve pool. Forty-six depeg events with a worst deviation of 291 bps positive shows the mechanism wobbles but recovers. The 3.61% yield from the Stability Pool carries a 0.20 yield-to-risk ratio, the best compensation-per-unit-of-risk in this batch. Primary-coverage DEX liquidity is concentrated at 0.52 HHI, meaning one pool failure would gut exit capacity. A clever design that works until vol overwhelms the leverage.

usdb-blast.title: Post-Airdrop Decay
usdb-blast.text: USDB's reserve is better than its reputation: 60% DAI/sDAI earning Maker's DSR yield, 25% USDC, 15% USDT -- quality stablecoin collateral that should produce a boring, functional dollar token. Instead, 1,346 depeg events and a worst deviation of -1030 bps tell the story of a rebasing stablecoin on a chain the market stopped caring about after the airdrop ended. Supply continues its slow bleed to $23.5M, down from $24.3M last month, while 1.3% APY from governance-set yield barely registers against a backdrop where money market rates are multiples higher. The C- safety grade at 53 is dragged down by Blast-only deployment with no redemption backstop and fallback-class DEX coverage, even though the underlying collateral would score well in any other wrapper. USDB is a technically competent product stranded on an island of diminishing relevance.

buidl-blackrock.title: The Stablecoin's Stablecoin
buidl-blackrock.text: BlackRock's BUIDL has crossed $3 billion in circulation and is growing fast -- up roughly 18% in the past month -- making it the largest tokenized money market fund and the asset that a growing list of stablecoins (USDe, USDtb, frxUSD, USD0, CASH) hold in their own reserves rather than managing T-bill custody directly. The B report card at 71 is a reminder that Pharos measures structural risk, not brand prestige: institutional-top custody at BNY Mellon and all-very-low-risk reserves earn A+ resilience, but zero DEX liquidity, zero public depeg events, and Reg D access restrictions confine BUIDL to a world invisible to retail. The ~3.5% NAV-appreciation yield net of 20 bps fees is T-bill rate pass-through, unremarkable on its own but compelling when you consider it comes with BlackRock counterparty risk rather than crypto-native smart contract risk. Eight chain deployments via Securitize are expanding the footprint, but BUIDL's true significance is infrastructural -- it is the plumbing layer where TradFi yield enters crypto's reserve stacks, not an asset most humans will ever hold directly.

btcusd-btcfi.title: Bitcoin's CDP Outpost
btcusd-btcfi.text: BtcUSD is backed 100% by overcollateralized Bitcoin in various wrapped forms — WBTC, BTCB, cbBTC, and native BTC — with alt-LST collateral quality classification reflecting the custody chains each wrapper adds. The peg score of 64 and over 1,000 depeg events including one that hit nearly 1,400 basis points make it one of the most frequently depegged CDPs per unit of market cap, though the DEWS Calm band at 15 suggests current conditions are stable. Deployed on Base and Bifrost with no modeled redemption backstop, the exit routes are limited to secondary market trading on chains the broader DeFi market doesn't heavily visit. The question remains whether BTC holders will trust yet another wrapping layer when established CDPs already accept wrapped Bitcoin with better liquidity and peg infrastructure.

usbd-bima.title: BTC Collateral, CDP Ambitions
usbd-bima.text: Bima's USBD puts Bitcoin liquid staking derivatives into Liquity-style vaults at 150% minimum collateral ratio, with permissionless redemption for $1 of BTC-denominated collateral and a PSM offering near-1:1 stablecoin swaps -- a sound architecture undermined by the quality of what sits inside. The NR safety grade, zero DEX liquidity, no observable price feed, and DEWS Alert at 38 paint the picture of a protocol that has not yet achieved escape velocity at $7.5M in stagnant supply across seven chains. The collateral is classified as alt-LST/bridged/mixed and rated high risk -- meaning this is not plain BTC backing but a chain of wrappers and restaking derivatives where each layer adds trust assumptions the Liquity mechanics were designed to avoid. The 83-rated permissionless redemption backstop is structurally strong on paper, but with zero secondary market and flatlined supply, the practical exit for most holders remains an open question.

isc-international-stable-currency.title: The Anti-Dollar Experiment
isc-international-stable-currency.text: ISC deliberately rejects the USD peg in favor of tracking purchasing power through a basket of gold, bonds, T-bills, equities, and cash — a flatcoin that appreciates over time rather than losing value to inflation, with NAV-based pricing and a 20% USDC dependency noted in its reserve structure. The institutional-unregulated custody and Solana-only deployment place ISC firmly in experimental territory, and the variable peg currency classification makes it harder to use as a medium of exchange than a conventional dollar token. As a concept, ISC is the most intellectually honest take on what 'stable' should mean — stable purchasing power rather than stable nominal value. At minimal market cap, ISC is about as niche as stablecoins get, proving that being philosophically right and being commercially viable are different things.

usd0-usual.title: Six Wrappers Deep
usd0-usual.text: USD0 is a stablecoin backed by stablecoins backed by stablecoins: Hashnote USYC, M by M0, Ethena's USDtb, BlackRock BUIDL, Ondo's OUSG, and Circle's USDC form a six-layer dependency chain where every wrapper adds counterparty risk that the B- safety grade at 68 can barely contain. Supply has flatlined around $556M after modest contraction from $559M last month, and DEWS sitting in the Watch band at 17 suggests the market hasn't forgotten the December 2024 USD0++ depeg that proved innovative tokenomics can undo even a diversified treasury-backed reserve. The 86-rated permissionless redemption backstop via DaoCollateral is the structural saving grace, but 38 depeg events and a worst deviation of -299 bps reveal a secondary market that periodically loses confidence in the wrapper stack. France-domiciled, RWA-backed, and architecturally ambitious, USD0 remains a bet that the sum of six low-risk parts doesn't compound into something meaningfully less safe than any individual component.

usr-resolv.title: Insurance Layer, Meet Reality
usr-resolv.text: Resolv's USR has collapsed to $0.164 -- an 83.6% deviation from its dollar peg -- earning an F report card score of 11 while the underlying safety grade sits at F/39, a gap that screams active crisis rather than chronic weakness. The RLP insurance layer that was supposed to absorb negative funding rates and protect USR holders has apparently been overwhelmed, with 25 depeg events including a worst of 9,025 basis points. Supply has been volatile, swinging from $17.5M last month to $28.4M last week to $22.3M today, the kind of oscillation that suggests frantic positioning rather than organic growth. The irony is sharp: Apostro real-time reserve verification and permissionless atomic redemption with an 82-rated backstop are still technically intact on a token trading at sixteen cents. Six-chain deployment across Ethereum, Base, BSC, Berachain, HyperEVM, and Arbitrum means this failure is visible everywhere, not just somewhere.

usdz-anzen.title: Private Credit Meets DeFi
usdz-anzen.text: Anzen's USDz is 80% backed by U.S. private credit ABS — SMB merchant receivables, factored invoices, auto leases, consumer installment lending, and litigation finance — underwritten by SEC-licensed broker-dealer Percent, with 15% in Superstate tokenized treasuries and 5% cash. The 559 depeg events and a peg score of 48 make USDz one of the most frequently depegged stablecoins on the dashboard, and supply has collapsed over 80% in a single month, answering the question of what happens when holders lose confidence in private credit backing. Qualified Market Makers mint at 1:1 USDz/USDC while retail relies on DEX arbitrage to close the gap — a two-tier system that works when the market trusts the collateral and breaks when it doesn't. The yield from private credit is real and uncorrelated with crypto markets, but so is the liquidity mismatch between 90-day receivables and instant redemption expectations.

ausd-agora.title: VanEck's Quiet Dollar
ausd-agora.text: Agora's AUSD deploys the kind of institutional firepower that most stablecoin issuers can only fantasize about: VanEck manages the reserves, State Street provides custody through a bankruptcy-remote Delaware Statutory Trust, and Chaos Labs delivers real-time proof of reserves on-chain -- a trust stack that earns a B+ report card at 79 with near-perfect peg stability and only 18 depeg events on record, none exceeding 191 basis points. The revenue-sharing model with distribution partners, where Agora splits reserve yield with platforms that drive adoption, has fueled aggressive expansion to 15 chains and over $125M in DEX liquidity across 62 pools with a healthy 0.12 concentration HHI. A DEWS score of just 5 in CALM territory and a 4.6% lending yield via Upshift with a B+ safety grade make AUSD one of the better-compensated risk profiles on the dashboard. The only tension is the familiar one: institutional-top custody and centralized issuance from Bermuda deliver excellent safety metrics everywhere except decentralization, where every centralized issuer collects its inevitable F.

usds-sky.title: The PSM Moat Deepens
usds-sky.text: Sky Dollar commands $8.6 billion in supply and the single best redemption infrastructure in stablecoins: a permissionless PSM with atomic settlement, zero fees, and nearly 50% of total supply available as immediate exit capacity -- no other stablecoin at scale offers anything close. The A safety grade at 84 reflects balanced strength across every dimension, with the reserve mix of 38% stablecoins via PSM, 28% Spark lending, and 23% Grove RWA providing genuine diversification rather than the concentration risk that plagues most competitors. At 3.75% APY through the Sky Savings Rate, the yield-to-risk ratio rewards holders without the exotic risk profiles that higher-yielding alternatives require. The structural dependency on USDC as mechanism-critical PSM collateral remains the one tension in a DAO-governed system that aspires to monetary sovereignty -- roughly a third of Sky Dollar's backing ultimately traces back to Circle's banking relationships.

m-m0.title: The Middleware Dollar
m-m0.text: M0's M token is backed 100% by short-term T-bills in bankruptcy-remote SPVs — a pristine reserve that now pairs a perfect peg score with a B- safety grade after Pharos modeled M0's offchain-issuer redemption backstop alongside thin DEX liquidity. The tension is still the same: direct M liquidity remains institution-facing, but eventual redeemability gives the token a stronger exit profile than spot pool depth alone would suggest. Permissioned Minters lock T-bill collateral while Validators cryptographically attest sufficiency on-chain, a trust architecture that replaces periodic auditor snapshots with protocol-level verification at the cost of institutional-unregulated custody and centralized governance. M's significance is downstream: it anchors the M0 infrastructure cohort that powers Noble's USDN, MetaMask's mUSD, USD.AI's USDai, Usual's USD0, and wrapped M integrations.

usdm-moneta.title: Peg in Name Only
usdm-moneta.text: Moneta's USDM has logged 1,656 depeg events with deviations as extreme as 18% below and 31% above its dollar peg, earning an F safety grade at 32 despite holding reserves that any regulator would applaud -- 60% money market funds from Fidelity and Amundi, 40% USD bank deposits, with a Norwegian MiCA EMT license and Charli3 oracle attestation before every mint. The problem is brutally simple: zero observable DEX liquidity on Cardano means there are no arbitrageurs to enforce the peg, so the price wanders wherever thin order books take it. The WATCH stress band at 18 and multi-day settlement window compound the exit risk for anyone holding meaningful size. USDM is the clearest case study in the dashboard for why pristine reserves are necessary but not sufficient -- without on-chain liquidity, a stablecoin is just a well-backed IOU trading at whatever the market feels like.

satusd-river.title: The Purist's CDP
satusd-river.text: River's satUSD makes a deliberate choice: no centralized stablecoin collateral accepted, only BTC, ETH, BNB, and LSTs — a principled stance that earns an A+ in dependency risk but costs it a peg score in the sixties with over 200 depeg events including one that hit nearly 4,500 basis points. The Omni-CDP architecture lets users deposit collateral on one chain and mint satUSD on another via LayerZero, spreading across eleven chains including some classified as unproven — a deployment breadth that triggers decentralization penalties despite the protocol's genuinely decentralized governance as a Liquity V1 fork. The 88-rated redemption backstop offers permissionless atomic access to blue-chip collateral, but with minimal DEX liquidity across all chains, the secondary market is paper-thin. satUSD is the most ideologically pure CDP at scale, but purity and peg stability have proven to be competing objectives.

usdf-astherus.title: One Exchange, One Exit
usdf-astherus.text: Astherus USDF routes its entire existence through Binance: 50% USDT held in Ceffu custody, 25% spot crypto longs, and 25% perpetual short positions -- all executed via Ceffu's MirrorX infrastructure on a single centralized exchange. The C+ safety grade at 64 with DEWS at 20 in the Watch band captures the concentration risk, while BSC-only deployment with $76K in DEX TVL from a single pool means on-chain exit options are essentially decorative. The 92-rated stablecoin redemption backstop with 50% immediate capacity sounds reassuring until you realize it depends on the same Binance-Ceffu pipeline that holds the collateral -- redundancy this is not. Supply has contracted 12% month-over-month from $134M to $118M under the Aster DEX rebrand, and three depeg events with modest deviations suggest the peg holds as long as Binance does. USDF is a delta-neutral yield product wearing a stablecoin's clothes, and the single point of failure is the entire wardrobe.

usda-avalon.title: The BTC-Backed Misnomer
usda-avalon.text: Avalon's USDa bills itself as Bitcoin-collateralized, but the reserve tells a different story: 45% FBTC via Cobo custody, 40% USDT minted 1:1, and 15% assorted BTC LSTs -- meaning the majority of backing is either a centralized stablecoin or a wrapped Bitcoin derivative with its own custody chain. Trading at $0.987 with 56 depeg events including a worst deviation of -2462 bps, USDa's C safety grade at 58 reflects the alt-LST collateral quality and centralized-dependent governance that the seven-chain distribution strategy can't disguise. DEWS at 33 in the Watch band and a liquidity score of just 12 with $156K effective TVL make this one of the thinnest major CDPs by secondary market depth. The 2.7% APY via sUSDa savings generates a negative yield-to-risk ratio, which is the market's way of saying the compensation doesn't match the complexity.

usdtb-ethena.title: The Load-Bearing Wall
usdtb-ethena.text: USDtb has grown to $939 million with a clear mandate: serve as the stable ballast inside Ethena's USDe reserve structure, where it constitutes the majority of backing for a multibillion-dollar synthetic dollar. The 90% BUIDL allocation channeled through Anchorage Digital under an OCC charter means the underlying assets are overwhelmingly U.S. Treasuries, yet the C+ safety grade at 62 reflects the layered counterparty chain -- from holder to USDtb to BUIDL to BlackRock to the actual bonds. Five depeg events with a worst deviation of 202 basis points and CALM stress suggest the product functions as intended, while $25.3 million in DEX TVL concentrated across just two pools on primary-class coverage confirms this is not optimized for retail DeFi composability. USDtb is a product designed to be held by its parent protocol rather than traded by individuals -- a perfectly rational design that nevertheless means most holders are exposed to Ethena's risk management decisions whether they realize it or not.

zeusd-zoth.title: Wrappers All the Way Down
zeusd-zoth.text: ZeUSD mints against a collateral stack of tokenized T-bills (USYC, STBT, TBILL), Usual's USD0++, and wrapped M — meaning every dollar of backing carries the risk profile of whichever upstream issuer is weakest in the chain. The F at 35 is the predictable result: Cayman domicile, no proof of reserves, institutional-unregulated custody, and a dependency chain where a failure in Hashnote, Matrixdock, or OpenEden cascades directly into ZeUSD's reserve. The $1,486 in DEX TVL across a single pool is not a liquidity problem — it is the absence of liquidity entirely, leaving $27.6M in circulating supply with no meaningful on-chain exit. Zero depeg events and a calm DEWS band mean the peg hasn't been tested, not that it would survive testing. The RWA-collateralized CDP model is architecturally interesting, but wrapping three layers of tokenized treasuries into a fourth token is the kind of financial engineering that works until it doesn't.

zchf-frankencoin.title: Oracle-Free Alpine Defiance
zchf-frankencoin.text: Frankencoin remains the most ideologically committed stablecoin on the dashboard — no foundation, no team tokens, no VC money, no price oracles — and the A- at 82 proves that decentralization orthodoxy can coexist with a functional safety profile. The collateral buffet of wrapped BTC, ETH derivatives, gold tokens, tokenized RWAs, and even CRV and GNO is valued through auction-based liquidation that trades capital efficiency for oracle manipulation resistance, a tradeoff most protocols wouldn't dare make. Four depeg events with tight deviations under 230 bps are remarkable for a CHF-pegged token priced against dollar reference rates on limited liquidity. The 3.5% APY from Frankencoin Savings on an A- safety grade produces a yield-to-risk ratio of 0.19 — genuinely attractive risk-adjusted return for a non-USD stablecoin. At 38.6M CHF circulating across Ethereum, Optimism, Gnosis, and Base, Frankencoin proves small protocols survive not despite their stubbornness but because of it.

usn-noon.title: Private Credit in a Stablecoin Wrapper
usn-noon.text: Noon's USN has shed the polite framing: 68.4% of its reserves sit in Fasanara private credit and another 13% in Janus Henderson JAAA CLOs, making this overwhelmingly a private credit vehicle that happens to be redeemable for USDC. The C+ safety grade at 60 and DEWS Calm score of 2 suggest operational stability, but the exotic collateral quality classification is earned -- barely 3.7% of reserves are in T-bills, with the rest split between CLOs, DeFi lending, and Pendle principal tokens. The 9.3% APY on sUSN has recovered from a period where yield dropped to zero, validating the rotating yield thesis while raising the question of which exotic sleeve is generating that return. Supply has dipped 13% month-over-month to $25.8M, and the five depeg events with a worst of 1,200 basis points positive suggest USN occasionally trades at a premium that nobody is arbitraging away.

honey-berachain.title: Proof of Liquidity's Dollar
honey-berachain.text: HONEY is Berachain's native stablecoin, minted 1:1 against a basket of USDC, USDT0, pyUSD, and USDe through permissionless on-chain vaults governed by BGT holders. The 85-rated redemption backstop with atomic settlement is the headline: you can always unwind HONEY into its constituent stablecoins, which is more than most basket tokens offer. But 35 depeg events including a +4,981 bps spike reveal the chaos beneath the surface -- that upward deviation suggests severe liquidity imbalances in the ecosystem's early days. At $25.6M circulating across 28 DEX pools, the concentration HHI of 0.30 shows reasonable liquidity distribution, though the effective TVL of just $879K relative to $10.2M total TVL signals much of that liquidity is shallow. The C safety grade is a direct tax on Berachain's unproven status; the underlying architecture would score meaningfully higher on an established chain.

wusd-worldwide.title: Enterprise Rails, Empty Station
wusd-worldwide.text: WSPN's Worldwide USD pairs a conservative reserve — T-bills and cash with a Basel III-inspired 6% liquidity buffer — against a B- grade at 68 that reflects the gap between institutional ambition and on-chain traction. The $335K DEX TVL across four pools on Ethereum, Polygon, and Viction is fallback-class liquidity for an $11.5M supply, and two depeg events with a worst of -182 bps suggest the peg holds but barely gets tested. The BVI domicile with FinCEN MSB registration is regulatory limbo: enough paperwork to look legitimate, not enough to satisfy institutional compliance departments shopping for USDC alternatives. WUSD's white-label infrastructure for enterprise stablecoin issuance is the real product pitch, but a payments network needs volume, and volume needs liquidity that isn't here yet.

frxusd-frax.title: Frax's Clean Slate
frxusd-frax.text: Where legacy FRAX carries 817 depeg events and a C grade, frxUSD launched as a do-over: 48% WisdomTree government money market, 37% Superstate USTB, 13% BlackRock BUIDL, and 2% DBS tokenized deposits, earning an A- safety grade with just 3 depeg events to date. The 93-rated atomic redemption backstop through enshrined custodians gives it one of the strongest exit routes in crypto-native stablecoins, and 71 DEX pools with a low 0.11 HHI show genuinely diversified liquidity across 24 chains. At $133M and growing, the sfrxUSD staking wrapper delivers 4.25% APY with a 0.14 yield-to-risk ratio against A- safety — modest but honest. The centralized-dependent governance model means Frax DAO retains the keys to custodian approvals, which is the one thread connecting this otherwise institutional-grade product to its wilder ancestry.

usyc-hashnote.title: Billions Without a Swap Pool
usyc-hashnote.text: Hashnote's USYC has swelled to $2.66 billion -- the largest tokenized Treasury product by circulation -- while maintaining exactly zero DEX pools and deployment on just two chains. The B- safety grade at 69 on a product backed entirely by T-bills and reverse repos continues to puzzle until you realize the score is penalizing everything the product deliberately doesn't do: decentralize, provide on-chain liquidity, or publish proof of reserves beyond its own API price feed. Supply grew 17% month-over-month from $2.27B, suggesting institutional demand that doesn't need or want DEX exit routes. At 3.19% APY via NAV appreciation (net of a 50% performance fee) and a token price of $1.12, USYC is functionally a Bermuda-licensed money market fund that happens to be an ERC-20 and a BEP-20. The Circle branding now appearing on its DefiLlama listing hints at strategic alignment that could eventually reshape how this product reaches the market.

eurr-stablr.title: Malta's Euro Bet
eurr-stablr.text: StablR's EURR is backed 100% by fiat euro at European financial institutions under a Malta MFSA EMI license with MiCA compliance and Grant Thornton attestations — the same regulatory infrastructure as its dollar sibling USDR, with Tether's strategic investment providing both capital and the awkward question of whether a Tether-backed entity can win institutional trust in a market built on regulatory purity. Ethereum-only deployment with institutional-regulated custody gives EURR clean infrastructure, but the euro stablecoin market remains a fraction of the dollar market, and competition from Circle's EURC, SocGen's EURCV, and Banking Circle's EURI means EURR must differentiate on something beyond compliance alone. The Tether connection is both asset and liability — distribution relationships and brand recognition offset by the regulatory scrutiny that follows Tether everywhere. Whether Malta's MFSA license carries the same weight as France's ACPR or the Netherlands' DNB in the MiCA credibility hierarchy remains the competitive question.

usdr-stablr.title: MiCA Compliant, Market Indifferent
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR holds a Malta MFSA EMI license under MiCA with 100% reserves in cash and short-term government bonds audited by Grant Thornton -- a regulatory stack that checks every European compliance box while the market barely notices at $6 million in supply. The WATCH stress band at 17 and 26 depeg events including a brutal 1,058-basis-point downside deviation reveal a single Ethereum pool with $1 million in TVL struggling to maintain any semblance of peg discipline. The liquidity score of 19 with perfect concentration in one pool means any meaningful exit runs through StablR's own issuer API rather than on-chain routes. Europe's MiCA framework was supposed to be the catalyst for regulated stablecoins, and USDR has the credentials to benefit -- but credentialing and adoption remain stubbornly separate problems at this scale.

usdo-openeden.title: Treasury Yield, Repackaged
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing stablecoin fixed at $1 that distributes T-bill yield daily by increasing holder balances — backed 70% by OpenEden's own TBILL tokens, 15% by BlackRock BUIDL, 5% by Franklin Templeton BENJI, and 10% in USDC as a cash buffer. The Bermuda BMA DABA license and Chainlink Proof of Reserves provide regulatory and transparency layers that most rebasing stablecoins lack, though the peg score of 81 and 44 depeg events — including one that spiked nearly 17,000 basis points above peg — reveal the mechanical challenge of maintaining a $1 price on a token whose supply changes daily. The backstop scores a modest 52 with capacity issues, reflecting the illiquidity gap between holding tokenized treasuries and providing instant dollar redemptions. Deployed across four chains, USDO is elegant for retail but awkward for DeFi protocols that don't handle rebasing tokens — hence the cUSDO wrapper for composability.

usda-anzens.title: Cardano's Lonely Dollar
usda-anzens.text: Anzens USDA offers the cleanest reserve on Cardano -- 60% USD cash, 40% U.S. Treasuries, all custodied by BitGo Trust under a FinCEN MSB license -- and the messiest peg record on the entire dashboard: 605 depeg events with deviations hitting -1704 bps on the downside and +2558 bps on the upside. The problem isn't the backing; it's the chain. A single DEX pool with $424K in TVL and Cardano-only deployment mean there is no meaningful arbitrage infrastructure to enforce the peg, producing a C safety grade at 56 despite reserves that would earn a much higher mark on any chain with real DeFi depth. Supply has shrunk 11% week-over-week to $9.5M, and the only exit is KYC-verified bank transfers through Anzens with multi-day settlement. USDA is proof that sound reserves are necessary but nowhere near sufficient -- you also need a market that can actually trade the thing.

usdf-falcon.title: Ethena's Wilder Cousin
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon Finance takes the delta-neutral playbook and cranks the risk dial: 45% BTC shorts, 30% stablecoins, 5% ETH shorts, 5% tokenized Treasuries, and the part that separates it from Ethena -- 15% in altcoins like DOGE, FET, TRX, and TON, each hedged with perp shorts on centralized exchanges where liquidity can vanish in a single cascade. At $1.79 billion in supply (up 2.6% weekly) with a B- safety grade at 68, Falcon has grown into a top-tier stablecoin by AUM while carrying exotic collateral quality and DEWS at 27 in the Watch band -- the only billion-dollar stablecoin persistently trading below peg at $0.998. The 5.7% sUSDf yield attracts capital, but the whitelisted-onchain redemption backstop scores just 65 with only 3.3% immediate capacity, meaning the exit door is narrow relative to the room's occupancy. Real-time reserve transparency via ht.digital is a genuine differentiator, though 37 depeg events and a worst deviation of -265 bps suggest the altcoin hedging strategy occasionally stumbles where BTC-only approaches wouldn't.

europ-schuman.title: Credentials Without Scale
europ-schuman.text: Schuman Financial stacks every credential the euro stablecoin market demands — ACPR EMI license from France, KPMG attestations, 98% of reserves in euro cash at Societe Generale and peer EU banks, a 2% buffer beyond par — and still sits at barely 8.6M EUR circulating, roughly the size of a mid-tier DeFi protocol's treasury. The B grade at 73 places EUROP in the same safety tier as EURC and Eurite, which is precisely the problem: when three euro stablecoins score identically on safety but differ by orders of magnitude in scale, the credentials become table stakes rather than differentiators. DEWS Watch at 20 and 28 depeg events with a worst drawdown of 229 bps reflect the thin-market volatility endemic to sub-$10M stablecoins, not structural instability. The five-chain deployment including XRPL and Plasma is an unusual distribution bet — reaching beyond EVM chains where the established euro competitors have not yet planted flags.

brz-transfero.title: Pegged to Volatility Itself
brz-transfero.text: BRZ's 184 depeg events -- including swings of nearly 10,000 basis points below peg and 7,800 above -- are not evidence of product failure but of what happens when you peg a token to the Brazilian real and price it against dollar-denominated markets. The D safety grade at 48 is largely a function of FX-driven peg volatility rather than reserve inadequacy, since BRZ is backed 100% by BRL cash at a Central Bank of Brazil-authorized institution with Swiss VQF registration. The practical exit story is grim: under $200K in effective DEX TVL across 14 pools, a 1% redemption fee through Transfero's offchain issuer path, and a liquidity score of 21 mean any position of size is essentially trapped until someone wants to buy it on the secondary market. Deployed across 14 chains with nearly 300 million reais in circulation, BRZ serves a genuine need in Latin America's largest crypto market -- but the DEWS Watch band at 29 and razor-thin liquidity are a standing reminder that non-USD stablecoins carry risks no reserve structure can hedge away.

rlusd-ripple.title: The Institutional On-Ramp
rlusd-ripple.text: Ripple's RLUSD has grown to $1.4B in circulation on just two chains, backed by a pristine 100% very-low-risk reserve split across T-bills, government money market funds, and cash under NYDFS supervision with BPM LLP attestations. The B+ report card at 75 and CALM stress band reflect the structural strength you'd expect, but the 54 depeg events -- including a 636 bps upward spike during early price discovery -- are a reminder that even well-collateralized tokens need time to build secondary market depth. DEX liquidity of $96M across only 4 pools (HHI 0.89) is heavily concentrated, which is consistent with RLUSD's design as a payments corridor token rather than a DeFi primitive. Supply dipped 8.5% from last month's $1.55B, suggesting institutional flows are lumpy rather than sticky -- the kind of pattern you see when a token is being used for settlement rather than held as a reserve asset.

feusd-felix.title: Liquity Fork on Hyperliquid
feusd-felix.text: Felix Protocol cloned Liquity V2 onto Hyperliquid's unproven L1 and loaded the CDPs with 60% HYPE ecosystem tokens — an asset class Pharos rates very-high risk — alongside bridged BTC, ETH, and SOL. The result is a $75M stablecoin with 339 depeg events and a worst deviation of 473 bps positive, currently trading at $0.994. The 93-rated redemption backstop is genuinely strong for a DeFi-native coin, with zero-fee atomic collateral redemption and an interest-rate-sorted queue. But the B safety grade tells the real story: when your primary collateral is the native token of the chain you live on, a single ecosystem shock hits both your backing and your exit liquidity simultaneously. Fifteen DEX pools rated fallback-class with 0.27 HHI concentration means getting out fast is not a given.

dusd-standx.title: The Quiet Basis Trader
dusd-standx.text: StandX runs the Ethena playbook through Ceffu custody with one critical difference: no governance token, no points program, no yield sharing — just a $99M delta-neutral stablecoin where 95% of reserves are active spot-long/perp-short positions on BTC, ETH, SOL, and BNB with a 5% stability buffer. The D grade at 49 is the honest assessment: CEX custody, exotic collateral, no published proof of reserves, and a redemption backstop scoring 57 via an issuer API with same-day settlement and only 5% immediate capacity. The peg record is actually clean — just 7 depeg events with the worst at 181 bps above peg — which suggests the Goldman Sachs and Binance Futures alumni running the desk know what they are doing, provided the infrastructure beneath them holds. DEWS Calm at 12 and stable supply near $99M say the market trusts the trade for now, but trust and verification are different things entirely.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen’s Blockchain Experiment
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EUR CoinVertible is issued by SG-FORGE, the digital asset arm of a systemically important European bank, with reserves held 100% in euro cash at Société Générale itself — institutional-top custody that earns the highest marks available in both resilience and dependency risk. The B safety grade makes EURCV one of the highest-rated euro stablecoins on Pharos, held back primarily by the expected F in decentralization — an inevitable trade-off when a 160-year-old bank decides to issue tokens on public blockchains. The DEWS stress reading is among the lowest on the entire dashboard, suggesting the product is operationally serene despite the thin DEX liquidity that plagues most euro stablecoins. Deployed across Ethereum, XRPL, Stellar, and Solana with MiCA EMI licensing from France’s ACPR, whether EURCV is the future of tokenized money or a corporate innovation lab’s pet project depends on whether SocGen commits distribution resources that match its regulatory credentials.

yusd-aegis.title: Funding Rate Roulette
yusd-aegis.text: Aegis YUSD is a delta-neutral stablecoin built entirely on BTC — spot long at Fireblocks, Copper, and Ceffu hedged by COIN-M perpetual shorts — which means the D grade at 46 is the market's verdict on using an active trading position as collateral. The 28 depeg events with a worst of -977 bps and +1705 bps tell the story of a token whose peg stability is a function of funding rate economics and exchange availability, not reserve quality. Real-time proof-of-reserves through Accountable is genuinely best-in-class transparency — you can watch the positions live, which is more than Ethena offers — but transparency doesn't reduce the underlying risk of CEX custody concentration. The 3.78% APY on a D-rated token produces a yield-to-risk ratio of 0.066, which is the market correctly pricing in the scenario where negative funding rates eat the insurance fund faster than it refills.

reusd-resupply.title: Leverage All the Way Down
reusd-resupply.text: Resupply's reUSD wraps Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares into a dollar token whose collateral is itself earning yield on other stablecoins -- turtles of leverage atop a 1% redemption fee floor. The C report card at 59 and 703 depeg events tell the tale of exotic collateral doing exotic things, though supply has stabilized around $35M after a slight contraction from last week's $37M. DEX liquidity is concentrated (HHI 0.59) across just 6 pools with an effective TVL of only $825K, meaning any serious exit would blow through the order book. The DEWS Watch band at 24 and a yield-to-risk ratio under 0.02 suggest the market correctly prices reUSD as a recursive instrument rather than a stable store of value -- you hold this to farm, not to park.

tbill-openeden.title: T-Bills With a Token Wrapper
tbill-openeden.text: OpenEden's TBILL holds $135M in short-dated Treasuries managed by BNY Investment Management with institutional-top custody, trading at $1.14 as accumulated NAV appreciation pushes the token further above its original dollar price. The B+ report card at 75 with zero depeg events and zero DEX pools is the signature of a KYC-gated fund structure that functions as intended: professional investors get 3.3% APY on-chain, and everyone else can look but not touch. Supply surged 67% from last month's $81M but pulled back from last week's $148M peak, showing the kind of institutional rebalancing flows that drive tokenized treasury products. The complete absence of secondary market liquidity is a feature, not a bug -- TBILL redeems through the issuer at a 5 bps fee with multi-day settlement, which is exactly how a regulated BVI fund should work.

a7a5-old-vector.title: The Sanctioned Dollar's Mirror
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is a ruble-pegged stablecoin backed 100% by deposits at Promsvyazbank — a Russian state-owned bank under Western sanctions — which is why Pharos classifies its custody as institutional-sanctioned and its reserve risk as very-high despite the collateral being plain fiat currency. Issued by Old Vector LLC under a Kyrgyz VASP license with quarterly audits from an independent Kyrgyz firm, the regulatory architecture is technically compliant with its home jurisdiction while being functionally untouchable by Western financial infrastructure. The issuer distributes 50% of reserve interest to holders as additional A7A5, making it one of the few stablecoins that pays yield from a sanctioned bank's deposit rates. Whether A7A5 represents financial innovation for an isolated economy or sanctions evasion with a token wrapper depends entirely on whose compliance framework you're applying.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: The Presidential Stablecoin
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 arrived with the Trump family brand and proved that political controversy does not prevent a stablecoin from functioning: 100% very-low-risk reserves in T-bills, money market funds, and cash, custodied by BitGo under a South Dakota trust charter. The irony is structural — USD1 is, by the numbers, a perfectly conventional stablecoin with impeccable reserves and a near-perfect peg score, indistinguishable from any Paxos or Circle product except for the name on the letterhead. Supply has contracted by double digits recently, suggesting that the initial burst of politically motivated minting is unwinding as holders discover that USD1 earns no yield and has thinner DEX liquidity than competitors half its size. Whether the brand is an asset or a liability depends on which side of the political aisle you mint from, but the B safety grade suggests the product itself is unremarkable in the best possible way.

usdx-hex-trust.title: Institutional Backing, Amateur Plumbing
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX has 80% T-bills and 20% cash at global tier-1 banks, which makes its D safety grade a case study in how clean reserves mean nothing without functional market infrastructure. Supply sits at $42.6M across three chains (Ethereum, Flare, Songbird), but the single DEX pool holding $200K with $836 in effective TVL is not a liquidity profile -- it's a rounding error. The 838 depeg events and a worst deviation of 7,191 basis points tell the story of a stablecoin that periodically trades at 28 cents on the dollar despite holding T-bills at par. DEWS has pulled back from Warning to Watch at 26, but that improvement just means the bleeding slowed, not that it stopped. Hong Kong TCSP licensing and 270+ institutional clients haven't translated into the on-chain arbitrage loops that keep prices honest, leaving USDX as expensive proof that custodial credibility and stablecoin stability are entirely different problems.

pusd-plume.title: USDC With a Detour
pusd-plume.text: Plume's pUSD takes USDC, routes it through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC compliance checks, and issues a wrapped token on Ethereum and Plume Chain -- adding smart contract risk, custody abstraction, and a new trust layer to an asset that was already perfectly functional. The C safety grade at 59 with zero-fee same-day redemption and CALM DEWS at 2 suggest the wrapper works as designed, but 15 depeg events including a catastrophic 4,049-basis-point negative deviation reveal at least one moment when it emphatically did not. Supply has drifted down 9% month-over-month to $6.1M with $258K in effective DEX liquidity, raising the question of whether the RWAfi ecosystem narrative generates enough demand to justify the wrapper's existence. pUSD is a solution in search of a problem that Plume hasn't yet proven it has.

bold-liquity.title: Immutable Code, Perfect Scores
bold-liquity.text: Liquity V2's BOLD is the highest-rated DeFi stablecoin on the dashboard, earning an A+ at 94 -- with a safety grade history that confirms this is structural, not a fluke. Backed by wstETH, WETH, and rETH in immutable contracts with no governance keys, no admin functions, and no RWA exposure, BOLD achieves what most decentralized stablecoins only aspire to: genuine peg stability alongside genuine decentralization, with just 6 depeg events recorded and none exceeding 134 basis points. The 90-rated redemption backstop with permissionless atomic collateral redemption at 50 bps provides the hardest peg floor in DeFi, while user-set interest rates and the Stability Pool yield mechanism (currently ~3.6% via Yearn's yBOLD) create self-correcting incentives that have kept BOLD remarkably close to par. Supply is growing modestly across seven chains, but the total remains small relative to the design's ambition -- proof that the market still prices convenience and composability above architectural purity.

avusd-avant.title: Avalanche's Quiet Contender
avusd-avant.text: Avant's avUSD is 95% backed by USDC deployed into delta-neutral strategies via 0xPartners, with a 5% loss-absorption reserve — structurally a USDC wrapper that earns yield through the savUSD vault while maintaining 1:1 redeemability at a 5-basis-point fee. The institutional-unregulated custody and BVI domicile mean the trust assumptions run through Avant's operational integrity rather than a regulatory framework, which is why the backstop scores a modest 68 with queue-based redemptions that can take one to seven days. Five depeg events including one that hit 321 basis points below peg suggest the peg mechanism isn't bulletproof under stress, though the peg score of 99 indicates these were brief anomalies.
