In the Avalanche ecosystem, being the default stable-value token with yield attached is a defensible position — the question is whether unregulated custody and a BVI entity are the right foundations for the scale Avant is targeting.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text: YLDS is that rarest of crypto products: a yield-bearing stablecoin registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Investment Company Act of 1940, paying SOFR minus 50 basis points through a fixed face-amount certificate structure that the SEC has explicitly blessed. The reserves are 86% overnight Treasury repos and 13% money market funds at UMB Bank, KPMG-audited, with institutional-top custody — a reserve stack so conservative it makes Circle look adventurous. Deployed on Solana and Provenance rather than Ethereum, YLDS targets a distribution path through Figure's existing lending platform rather than DeFi composability. The trade-off is clear: full SEC registration means mandatory KYC, restricted transferability, and zero DeFi integration, but for institutions that need a yield product whose legal status doesn't require a creative memo from outside counsel, YLDS is the only game in town.

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ holds the distinction of being supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank under MiCAR with reserves maintained at 102% overcollateralization — 69% in Netherlands, German, and U.S. government bonds with 31% in cash at Tier 1 European banks, all held in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts. A perfect peg score of 100 with zero depeg events and zero redemption fees makes USDQ the cleanest-performing USD stablecoin outside the top ten by every stability metric Pharos tracks. Deployed across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL, and Algorand, the distribution is modest but the regulatory positioning is unmatched: DNB supervision, MiCAR compliance, and a Visa principal membership for stablecoin-linked debit cards turn compliance into competitive advantage. Whether the Dutch compliance premium translates into adoption at scale depends on whether European crypto users value regulatory certainty enough to choose USDQ over the familiar convenience of USDC.

usdn-noble.title: Cosmos Dollar, Shrinking
usdn-noble.text: Noble Dollar has shed nearly half its supply in a month, dropping from $25 million to $13.4 million, a trajectory that undercuts the bullish thesis for an IBC-native rebasing stablecoin backed 100% by T-bills in bankruptcy-remote SPVs via M0. The B safety grade at 70 reflects solid fundamentals -- only 2 depeg events, CALM stress, real-time reserve verification through M0's dashboard -- but $26,000 in DEX TVL across a single pool with perfect concentration is barely a rounding error. The rebasing mechanism that passes T-bill yield directly to holders is an elegant design that should theoretically drive adoption, yet the supply contraction suggests Cosmos ecosystem demand alone cannot sustain it. Noble's proven IBC infrastructure has moved billions in USDC transfers, but USDN needs a reason for those dollars to stay as USDN rather than passing through.

usdu-unitas.title: The JLP Hedge Fund
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens — a basket of BTC, ETH, SOL, and USDC earning Jupiter Perps trading fees — while hedging the spot exposure with CEX perpetual shorts through Copper and Ceffu off-exchange settlement. The remaining 20% sits as margin for the short positions, making the entire reserve an active trading strategy with exotic collateral quality classification and zero idle assets. Singapore-domiciled with Accountable providing real-time zero-knowledge solvency proofs, USDu's transparency is a genuine upgrade over the 'trust us' school of yield products. Deployed on BSC and Solana with a peg score of 99 and only six depeg events, the machinery works — but the 80% dependency on USDC means every dollar of backing passes through Circle before reaching Jupiter's perps market, adding a layer of counterparty risk the hedge fund framing might obscure.

mnee-mnee.title: BSV Refugee, T-Bill Convert
mnee-mnee.text: MNEE wraps 85% short-dated Treasuries and 15% cash into a clean reserve profile attested by Wolf and Company -- the kind of composition that earns an A+ dependency score and a peg score of 97. The B- safety grade at 69 is a product of infrastructure, not reserves: Antigua FSRC licensing, institutional-unregulated custody, and a single Ethereum deployment with effectively $17K in usable DEX liquidity leave holders dependent on issuer-API redemption as the only credible exit. Sixteen depeg events including a 601-basis-point plunge expose what happens when a $101M stablecoin has no on-chain arbitrage infrastructure to defend parity. MNEE proved a fiat-backed coin can have pristine reserves and still score like a mid-tier product when the plumbing around it is this thin.

usdg-paxos.title: Paxos's Singapore Sequel
usdg-paxos.text: After Binance's BUSD died under regulatory fire, Paxos relocated its stablecoin ambitions to Singapore, where USDG now sits under a MAS Major Payment Institution license with reserves split between DBS Bank and Standard Chartered — institutional-top custody that matches Circle and exceeds Tether. The all-very-low-risk reserve composition and A+ resilience grade make USDG structurally one of the safest stablecoins in existence, which makes the lowest peg score among rated top-ten coins a curious anomaly — a brief tracking history with early growing pains rather than structural fragility. The zero-fee redemption and additional EU issuance via a MiCA-compliant Finnish entity give USDG a dual-jurisdiction strategy that no competitor currently matches. The catch is on-chain presence: concentrated on just a few chains with modest DEX depth, USDG's institutional pedigree still outpaces its DeFi footprint.

xsgd-straitsx.title: Southeast Asia's FX Shortcut
xsgd-straitsx.text: XSGD is the rare non-USD stablecoin that exists for a reason beyond novelty — SGD-denominated on-chain liquidity for Southeast Asian payment flows where routing through dollar pairs adds pointless FX friction. The B+ at 76 is earned: MAS Major Payment Institution license, 100% reserves at DBS and Standard Chartered, and twice-monthly independent attestations to ISCA standards. Twenty-five depeg events with a worst of -733 bps and +1265 bps look alarming until you account for the inherent pricing challenges of a SGD token valued against USD-denominated oracles on thin non-USD pairs. The $1.76M DEX TVL across 24 pools with an impressively low 0.129 HHI shows genuine liquidity diversification, and the Grab partnership and OKX Pay integration push XSGD into real payment corridors where most stablecoins only write blog posts about going.

xusd-straitsx.title: Good Bones, No Tenants
xusd-straitsx.text: StraitsX's XUSD inherits the same MAS framework, DBS/StanChart/UOB custody, and institutional-top infrastructure as its XSGD sibling, yet the B+ at 75 masks a liquidity crisis: $225K in DEX TVL with a 0.971 HHI means one pool holds essentially everything, and the 123 depeg events confirm what thin markets produce. The $50M circulating supply is respectable for a Singapore-issued dollar stablecoin, but it lives almost entirely off-chain — the on-chain footprint on Ethereum and BSC is a ghost town. XUSD's zero DEWS stress score and solid redemption backstop at 65 confirm the institutional plumbing works fine; the problem is that nobody building in DeFi has a reason to choose it over USDC. The value proposition is regional FX corridors and StraitsX's banking relationships, not DEX composability — a perfectly valid business, just not one that shows up in on-chain metrics.

vgbp-vnx.title: The Loneliest Pound
vgbp-vnx.text: VGBP occupies one of the emptiest niches in stablecoins: on-chain British sterling, where the competition is essentially nobody. At 172K GBP circulating on Base and Celo with $33K in DEX TVL, this is less a stablecoin and more a proof of concept that GBP can exist on-chain at all. The AREVA-audited reserves at Swiss and Liechtenstein banks under FMA TVTG licensing provide more regulatory infrastructure than the token's market presence would seem to justify, and the DEWS Watch band at 18 flags thin-market fragility rather than reserve concern. The UK's stablecoin regulatory framework remains the wildcard — if it invites high-street banks to issue tokenized sterling, VGBP's first-mover advantage evaporates overnight. Until then, VNX holds the field by default in a market nobody has shown up to contest.

cusd-cap.title: The Stablecoin Basket Case
cusd-cap.text: Cap's cUSD is a basket wrapper backed by 35% USDC, 25% USDT, 20% BlackRock's BUIDL, 10% Franklin Templeton's BENJI, and 10% PayPal's PYUSD — five institutional-grade stablecoins blended into a single token with a maximum 40% concentration cap per asset. The dynamic-fee vault mechanism adjusts minting and redemption costs in real-time to prevent full utilization, ensuring atomic redemptions remain available, while EigenLayer AVS provides the economic security layer. Redemptions return a proportional basket of all underlying assets rather than a single stablecoin, which socializes any individual reserve depeg across all redeemers — clever risk distribution if everything works, shared contagion if one component fails. Ethereum-only deployment and wrapper-classified governance mean cUSD is less an independent stablecoin and more a diversification instrument for holders who want institutional RWA exposure without choosing sides.

msusd-main-street.title: Options Desk in Stablecoin Clothing
msusd-main-street.text: Main Street USD is a USDC wrapper that routes reserves into delta-neutral options box spreads on centralized exchanges, delivering nearly 12% APY -- a figure that should make anyone fluent in risk-free rates raise an eyebrow. The B- safety grade at 69 marks a notable upgrade from its former C- rating, though CEX custody and exotic collateral quality remain the structural weak points. Supply has surged 38% in a month to $47M, suggesting the yield is attracting capital faster than the risk framework has matured. The 92-rated backstop via permissionless atomic USDC redemption is the genuine saving grace: holders can exit at par on-chain regardless of what the options book is doing. Seventeen depeg events and a worst positive deviation of 527 bps reveal price discovery is still rough around the edges -- the kind of volatility that separates yield-seekers from yield-survivors.

iusd-infinifi.title: Credit Fund in Token Clothing
iusd-infinifi.text: InfiniFi's iUSD deploys USDC reserves into institutional private credit -- Fasanara, FalconX, Sentora, Maple -- with a liquid DeFi buffer on Spark, Fluid, and Aave to service redemptions, paying 5.78% APY through its siUSD savings wrapper. The structural tension is immediate: only 19.6% of reserves are available for instant withdrawal, meaning four-fifths of the backing is locked in credit strategies with 30-day unwind windows. Supply has contracted sharply from $173M to $109M in a single month, a 37% drawdown that tests whether the fractional liquid reserve model actually works under redemption pressure. The WATCH-band DEWS score of 18 and B safety grade at 70 reflect this managed stress -- the yield-to-risk ratio of 0.12 is competitive, but you're earning credit fund returns and bearing credit fund risks through a stablecoin interface. No depeg events recorded yet, which either means the queue system is working exactly as designed or that the real stress test hasn't arrived.

pht-pht.title: Peso Stablecoin Pioneer
pht-pht.text: PHT is a Philippine peso-pegged stablecoin built on a MakerDAO MCD fork, backed 100% by apcxUSDT (a 1:1 custodial USDT wrapper) in CDP vaults with Chainlink oracle price feeds — Singapore-domiciled with institutional-regulated custody. The reserve is technically high-risk not because USDT is unstable but because the apcxUSDT wrapper adds a custodial layer between PHT holders and the underlying Tether. Targeting the $38 billion Filipino remittance corridor where traditional fees eat 6%+ of every transfer, the use case is compelling but adoption requires merchant integration and fiat off-ramps that raw DeFi infrastructure doesn't provide. Ethereum-only deployment and the MCD fork architecture are battle-tested, but PHT remains a worthy experiment proving that local-currency stablecoins for emerging markets need distribution more than they need innovation.

hyusd-hylo.title: Staked SOL, Stable Dollar
hyusd-hylo.text: Hylo's hyUSD converts Solana staking yield into dollar stability through a dual-token design where xSOL absorbs SOL's volatility so hyUSD doesn't have to -- backed entirely by a basket of liquid staking tokens (mSOL, JitoSOL, bSOL, JupSOL) at 150%+ overcollateralization with no upstream stablecoin dependencies. The B safety grade at 70 with only three depeg events (worst: -171 bps) is a quietly remarkable result for a stablecoin whose entire backing is volatile crypto. DAO governance and the absence of admin keys earn genuine decentralization marks, a rarity among crypto-backed competitors. The WATCH-band DEWS at 19 and a slight monthly supply contraction from $17M to $15.5M suggest Hylo is in a consolidation phase rather than a growth one, while $3.1M in DEX TVL across six pools provides adequate but not deep exit liquidity for the current supply. Oracle-free and admin-free is an elegant thesis -- the question is whether the Solana LST ecosystem remains healthy enough to keep the collateral basket liquid.

meusd-mezo.title: Bitcoin Maxis Get CDPs
meusd-mezo.text: Mezo's meUSD applies Liquity-style CDP mechanics to Bitcoin collateral -- 110% minimum ratio, permissionless redemption at 75 bps, atomic settlement -- across wrapped BTC variants on a Bitcoin L2 that Pharos classifies as unproven. The C+ grade at 63 with an 87-rated backstop tells a split story: the redemption architecture is sound, but the unproven chain penalty caps the ceiling on what is otherwise a competently designed system. At $18.9M circulating with 184 depeg events and a worst positive deviation of +504 bps, meUSD exhibits the above-peg drift typical of BTC-backed CDPs -- borrowers overcollateralize defensively when Bitcoin volatility spikes, pushing the token above par. DEWS reads a calm 13 and supply has been flat for months, suggesting meUSD has found its equilibrium as a niche product for BTC holders who want dollar-denominated leverage without selling their stack. The two-chain deployment across Ethereum and Mezo is pragmatic, though $4.9M in DEX liquidity spread across seven pools remains thin for any serious exit scenario.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: Undercollateralized by Design
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU Finance is refreshingly honest about what it is: an intentionally undercollateralized stablecoin at roughly 43% backing, minted through DAO-approved adapters connected to Curve, TermMax, and Morpho vault positions, designed explicitly for professional market participants who can price the risk. The C safety grade at 55 with $31,000 in DEX TVL and 84% pool concentration in a single venue means exit liquidity is essentially nonexistent for any meaningful position. Supply has been flat at $5 million for weeks, suggesting the professional audience it targets has sized their exposure and stopped. The modular adapter architecture is genuinely interesting engineering -- dynamic Curve liquidity management, fixed-rate TermMax lending, Morpho vault integration -- but building sophisticated infrastructure around a product that deliberately skips the overcollateralization step is the kind of experiment that works until it doesn't.

uty-xsy.title: Frozen on the Avalanche
uty-xsy.text: XSY's UTY hasn't moved in a month -- supply is $20.97M, identical to the penny across weekly and monthly snapshots, the kind of flatline that suggests a product in stasis rather than operation. The F safety grade at 37 pairs with a DEWS Watch score of 17, up from the previous zero, indicating that even dormant products can accumulate stress signals. The delta-neutral AVAX strategy (35% long spot, 35% short perps, 30% USDC) is custodied at Ceffu and Copper with Accountable attestations, but the 7-day unbonding period and fallback-class DEX coverage at $8.3M total TVL with $730K effective make exit an exercise in patience. Thirty-five depeg events with a worst of 287 basis points positive and 110 negative are relatively contained for an F-rated coin, suggesting the peg mechanism works when anyone bothers to test it. UTY reads less like a stablecoin and more like a locked vault on a quiet mountain.

gusd-gate.title: Exchange Scrip, Treasury Wrapper
gusd-gate.text: Gate USD functions less as a stablecoin and more as a yield certificate: users deposit USDT or USDC on Gate, receive GUSD, and reclaim principal plus interest at redemption. The reserve is 70% short-term Treasuries and 25% stablecoin deposits, but that final 5% in undisclosed CEX-managed yield strategies is the opacity that drags the safety grade to C. At $158M circulating from the Cayman Islands with exactly one DEX pool (HHI of 1.0 — maximum possible concentration), the on-chain exit route is effectively decorative. Nine depeg events with a tight 171 bps worst deviation suggest the peg mechanism works, but only because almost nobody tries to exit through DeFi. The 65-rated offchain redemption via Gate's own platform means your exit depends entirely on the exchange remaining operational and willing.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: TradFi's On-Chain Experiment
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: USDCV is what happens when Europe's sixth-largest bank decides to issue a stablecoin: 100% USD cash at BNY Mellon in bankruptcy-remote segregated accounts, an ACPR-regulated EMI license under MiCA, institutional-top custody, and a DEWS score of 1 -- literally the calmest stress reading on the entire Pharos dashboard. The B safety grade at 72 is held back not by risk but by reach: $26M in supply, a single DEX pool with $2.3M TVL, two-chain deployment on Ethereum and Solana, and multi-day settlement through SG-FORGE's issuer portal. Only 2 depeg events in its lifetime and a worst negative deviation of just -118 bps make it one of the most stable assets tracked, period. Supply grew 13% month-over-month from $23.3M, suggesting the MiCA framework is starting to drive institutional demand for a product whose on-chain liquidity still hasn't caught up with its regulatory pedigree.

usdai-usd-ai.title: The Liquid Half of USD.AI
usdai-usd-ai.text: Base USDai is the low-risk side of the USD.AI stack: a liquid, non-yielding token that current issuer materials frame around a PYUSD-led settlement rail rather than around the GPU-credit book itself. That distinction matters. The queue, the AI-infrastructure yield, and the GPU-loan underwriting risk belong to sUSDai, not to the base token holders using USDai as a transactional dollar. The remaining question is operational rather than conceptual: how durable the PYUSD-side redemption rail stays under stress, and how tightly the market continues to trust the separation between the liquid stablecoin layer and the higher-risk yield layer sitting beside it.

susdai-usd-ai.title: The GPU-Credit Sleeve
susdai-usd-ai.text: sUSDai is where USD.AI stops behaving like a plain stablecoin and starts looking like a structured credit product wrapped in token form. Holders are opting into yield sourced from GPU-backed infrastructure loans and accepting the trade-off that exits are governed by a queued unstake flow rather than the base token's instant redeem rail. The reserve mix still includes a large PYUSD sleeve, which softens liquidity management, but the defining exposure is the private compute-financing book. That makes sUSDai less a digital cash instrument than a NAV-style income token whose real question is how resilient that GPU-credit pipeline remains through borrower stress, collateral liquidation, and scaling cycles.

usx-solstice.title: The Solana Wrapper
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX is structurally simpler than its Swiss pedigree and Galaxy Digital backing might suggest: 55% USDC and 45% USDT, minted 1:1, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve verifying the reserves on-chain. Classified as a wrapper with governance quality reflecting its pass-through nature, USX inherits the safety profile of its underlying stablecoins rather than creating its own — which makes the value proposition a question of Solana-native convenience rather than novel design. The KYC-gated institutional minting at a $500K minimum coexists with permissionless DEX access, creating a two-tier system where large minters get direct access and everyone else trades the secondary market. Plans to expand collateral to SOL, ETH, and BTC would change the risk profile entirely, but for now USX is a regulated stablecoin wrapper on a chain that already has USDC and USDT.

hollar-hydrated.title: Aave Fork, Polkadot Address
hollar-hydrated.text: HOLLAR is an Aave V3 fork running on Hydration, Polkadot's largest DeFi protocol, backed by a diversified basket of DOT, ETH, vDOT, wrapped BTC, and stablecoins with automated partial liquidations that fire every block. The C grade at 55 has improved since launch, while the Stability Module's backstop design earns structural marks -- but everything runs on a chain Pharos classifies as unproven, which anchors the ceiling. At $11.7M circulating and gently contracting (down 4% monthly), HOLLAR isn't growing so much as stabilizing in place, with $2.7M in DEX liquidity concentrated entirely in a single pool. Seven depeg events with a worst deviation of -691 bps show the peg holds most of the time but can slip when liquidity thins. HOLLAR's viability ultimately tracks whether Polkadot's DeFi ecosystem expands or contracts -- a bet that has not paid off for most Polkadot-native projects to date.

musd-metamask.title: Distribution as Moat
musd-metamask.text: MetaMask mUSD is what happens when a wallet with 30 million monthly users decides to vertically integrate -- issued by Stripe's Bridge on M0 protocol rails, with 85% in T-bills and 15% in bankruptcy-remote cash verified by real-time on-chain validators. The B safety grade at 70 reflects solid fundamentals: DEWS at a tranquil 5, institutional-regulated custody, and a reserve composition that reads like a compliance team's wishlist. Supply has climbed 19% month-over-month to $32M, still modest for a product with that distribution funnel, but the trajectory is clear. Nineteen depeg events including a 557-bps positive spike and 236-bps negative deviation show the secondary market hasn't caught up with primary market confidence -- $2.5M in effective DEX TVL across 21 pools means mUSD's liquidity is spread wide but runs shallow.

cash-phantom.title: The Wallet's Dollar
cash-phantom.text: Phantom's CASH leverages what no DeFi protocol can replicate: distribution through crypto's most popular Solana wallet, giving millions of users a native stablecoin without requiring them to understand anything about stablecoin infrastructure. Under the hood, Bridge Building Inc. backs CASH with T-bills, reverse repos, government money-market funds, bank deposits, and a 10% allocation to tokenized treasuries including BUIDL -- 90% of reserves in very-low-risk assets with bankruptcy-remote segregation under FinCEN and state money transmitter licenses. The B- report card at 67 with just 10 depeg events (none exceeding 181 bps) and a DEWS score of 11 in CALM territory reflects a genuinely stable product, while over $72M in DEX liquidity across Solana pools provides workable exit depth. Solana-only deployment is a feature, not a limitation -- CASH exists to be Phantom's default dollar, and the growing supply suggests that for wallet-native users, the trade-off between decentralization purity and tap-to-buy convenience was decided before it was ever offered.

tgbp-tokenised.title: The FCA's First Bet
tgbp-tokenised.text: BCP Technologies' tGBP remains the UK's first FCA-registered stablecoin, backed 100% by GBP cash and zero-coupon gilts with Enumis custody across six chains -- but at 15.8M GBP in circulation, it is still a regulatory proof-of-concept in a dollar-denominated world. The B- report card at 69 with a DEWS Watch band at 25 reflects decent fundamentals constrained by scale: 24 depeg events with a worst miss of 265 bps and $1.4M in DEX TVL spread thinly across 9 pools. Supply grew 43% from last month's 11M GBP, which is notable momentum for a non-USD peg that most of DeFi ignores entirely. tGBP's significance remains less about today's numbers and more about the regulatory precedent -- every UK stablecoin issuer that follows will be benchmarked against this template.

eurau-allunity.title: Deutsche Boerse's Euro Bet
eurau-allunity.text: AllUnity's EURAU is backed 100% by euro deposits at CRR-eligible EU credit institutions, BaFin-licensed as an EMI under MiCA, with institutional-regulated custody and integration into Deutsche Boerse's Clearstream infrastructure — more institutional credibility than most euro stablecoins combined. Backed by DWS (Deutsche Bank's asset management arm), Galaxy Digital, and Flow Traders, the sponsor list reads like a TradFi-crypto bridge roster. Deployed across five EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon), EURAU has broader L2 reach than competing euro stablecoins that remain Ethereum-only. The problem is the denominator: euro stablecoins represent a fraction of the global stablecoin market, making EURAU simultaneously one of the best-backed euro tokens and a reminder of how thoroughly the dollar dominates this space.

usdh-native-markets.title: Stripe's Stablecoin Beachhead
usdh-native-markets.text: USDH sits at $94 million on HyperEVM with one of the more credible reserve compositions in the market: 40% short-term T-bills managed by BlackRock at JP Morgan, 20% tokenized treasuries via BUIDL and USTB, and the rest in cash, repos, and treasury funds -- all flowing through Bridge Building Inc., Stripe's stablecoin subsidiary. The 12 depeg events with swings as wide as 227 basis points tell the story of a young stablecoin on a single chain still building the arbitrage infrastructure to enforce its peg tightly. A 7.8% APY on Morpho lending at B- safety is a respectable yield-to-risk ratio, though the fallback-class DEX liquidity and concentrated pool structure mean size limits on exits remain real. The validator vote that chose USDH over Paxos and Ethena was a bet on revenue redirection from Circle -- whether that bet pays off depends on whether Hyperliquid's ecosystem grows beyond its current niche.

sbc-brale.title: Infrastructure Demo Reel
sbc-brale.text: Brale's SBC tripled from $3.9M to $12.2M in the past month -- the fastest proportional growth in this batch -- while maintaining a B safety grade at 73 with 100% very-low-risk reserves split evenly between cash and short-duration Treasuries. Deployed across 10 chains from a FinCEN-licensed money transmitter, SBC has broader distribution than tokens fifty times its size, which is entirely the point: this is a reference implementation for Brale's stablecoin-as-a-service platform, not a consumer product. The 35 depeg events with a worst deviation of 450 bps and an effective DEX TVL of just $5M against that 10-chain footprint reveal the tension between distribution breadth and liquidity depth. SBC exists so Brale can tell enterprise clients their infrastructure works -- and the tripling supply suggests those conversations are landing.

euri-banking-circle.title: The Binance Distribution Play
euri-banking-circle.text: Eurite exists because Binance needed a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin and Banking Circle had the Luxembourg CSSF credit institution license to provide one — 70% euro cash in segregated fiduciary accounts, 30% EU government securities, Ernst & Young attestations, all the regulatory furniture arranged correctly. The B grade at 73 matches the euro stablecoin peer group exactly, though the liquidity score of 33 and an HHI of 0.82 reveal the gap between having Binance's endorsement and generating organic on-chain trading depth. Supply has held flat week-over-week at roughly 60M EUR while growing about 9% over the prior month, suggesting institutional minting in discrete blocks rather than organic retail demand. No depeg data, no yield product, deployment limited to Ethereum and BSC — Eurite is less a standalone stablecoin and more a compliance wrapper that lets Binance's European users stay in euros without leaving the exchange's orbit.

msusd-metronome.title: Synths Still Standing
msusd-metronome.text: Metronome's msUSD is a synthetic dollar from the pre-yield-farming era that somehow kept its users — minted against 30% USDC, 25% Vesper yield tokens, 20% DAI, and 20% ETH/WBTC/sfrxETH, with no direct redemption mechanism, only debt repayment. The C+ safety grade at 62 with balanced B+ scores across peg stability, liquidity, and resilience is remarkably consistent for a product this niche, though the B- in dependency risk reflects exposure to DAI, USDC, and the legacy FRAX in its collateral basket. Supply has spiked over 40% in a single week — an unusual surge for a synthetic asset that most of DeFi has forgotten about, suggesting renewed interest or a single large minter. The zero-slippage intra-protocol synth swaps remain a neat trick in a market where synthetic assets have largely fallen out of fashion, and the 63-day peg streak shows the collateral-provider buyback mechanism is doing its job.

aznd-mu-digital.title: Asia Credit in a Token
aznd-mu-digital.text: Mu Digital's AZND wraps an Asian credit fund into a yield-bearing stablecoin on Monad, managed by Singapore-regulated Golden Hill Asset Management with a muBOND junior tranche providing overcollateralization -- it is a structured credit product wearing a stablecoin's clothing. Accountable's real-time dashboard currently shows reserves concentrated in short-term cash (81%) and liquid bonds (19%), a notably more conservative posture than the published mandate targeting up to 20% illiquid private credit. The B- report card at 67 with a 6.8% NAV-appreciation yield is credible for the risk class, though the single-chain Monad deployment, concentrated DEX liquidity (HHI of 0.72 across just 2 pools), and weekly KYC-gated redemptions settling over days mean exit options are genuinely constrained. Supply has contracted roughly 20% in the past week alone, suggesting early holders are testing those redemption mechanics in practice. AZND targets a real gap -- institutional Asian credit exposure on-chain -- but the question is whether DeFi-native capital will accept fund-style lockups for single-digit yields.

nect-beraborrow.title: Liquity on Life Support
nect-beraborrow.text: BeraBorrow's NECT runs Liquity-v2 mechanics on Berachain's exotic collateral zoo -- 40% iBGT, 25% WBERA, plus wrapped BTC variants, ETH derivatives, and Kodiak LP tokens, all classified high-risk on an unproven chain. The C- grade at 52 understates the challenge: 245 depeg events with a worst deviation of 757 bps mean NECT has spent more time away from peg than on it, though DEWS has calmed to 5 from its former Alert-band reading. At $512K in circulation with $246K effective DEX liquidity, the coin is barely above the threshold where the CDP redemption mechanism can function as designed -- you need arbitrageurs to show up, and the economics don't justify it at this scale. The 84-rated collateral redemption backstop remains structurally sound on paper, but sound mechanisms need liquid markets to express themselves.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token — 50% deployed into a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy via Balsa Technologies (delta-neutral TRY/USD trades capturing Turkey's inflation-driven carry), 40% across DeFi protocols (Giza, Almanak, USD.AI, Ethena, Aave, Cap), and 10% in a USDC/USDT buffer. The very-high risk classification on the Turkish FX strategy and high risk on the DeFi allocations are reflected in the exotic collateral quality rating and a backstop of 65 with whitelisted queue-based redemptions at 0.2% fee — KYC/KYB required to mint or redeem, with a 24-hour FIFO settlement queue. It's a genuinely novel yield source for DeFi — Turkish carry trade returns are uncorrelated with crypto markets — but also one that concentrates geopolitical and counterparty risk in a single emerging market whose currency has lost over 90% against the dollar in a decade. The NAV has appreciated above $1.07, which proves the strategy works when it works — the question is what happens when it doesn't.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Commodity Peg, Dollar Problem
pmusd-precious-metals.text: RAAC's pmUSD demonstrates why backing a dollar-pegged stablecoin with gold is an exercise in structural contradiction: 419 depeg events -- more than one per day of its existence -- and a D safety grade at 44 tell the story of a mechanism that must continuously absorb gold price movements to maintain a USD peg. Trading at $0.993 with DEWS in the Watch band at 26, the coin has shed 9% of supply month-over-month to $99M while the no-backstop designation means Pharos models no credible exit route at par. The transparency infrastructure is genuinely impressive -- real-time Chainlink Proof of Reserves and Instruxi attestations on 100% ION.au tokenized gold -- but transparency about a structurally challenged mechanism doesn't fix the mechanism. Gold is a fine store of value; it is a terrible peg anchor for a dollar stablecoin.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Three Layers to Treasuries
jupusd-jupiter.text: JupUSD is Jupiter's play to own Solana's dollar layer: 90% backed by Ethena's USDtb (itself a wrapper around BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized Treasury fund) with a 10% USDC buffer, custodied by Anchorage Digital. The dependency chain runs JupUSD to USDtb to BUIDL to actual government bonds -- pristine collateral buried under three layers of operational and counterparty risk. At $80M circulating and growing 11% month-over-month, adoption is real, with $12M in DEX TVL though heavily concentrated (HHI of 0.71) in a few pools. Eight depeg events with modest deviations (-202 to +158 bps) and a calm DEWS of 11 suggest a clean launch, while the 79-rated backstop offers atomic settlement through whitelisted on-chain redemption into stablecoins. The C+ grade at 63 prices in the dependency complexity and centralized governance -- Jupiter is betting that BlackRock's brand travels well enough through intermediaries that Solana users won't mind the wrapper tax.

u-united-stables.title: A Dollar Made of Dollars
u-united-stables.text: United Stables wraps 35% USDC, 35% USDT, 15% World Liberty Financial's USD1, and 15% fiat into a single token -- a meta-stablecoin approaching $1B in circulation that adds BVI custody risk on top of assets that already work fine on their own. The B- report card at 65 with zero depeg events and a CALM stress band at 11 reflects the paradox: the underlying collateral is solid, but the wrapper's unregulated Bermuda trustee and centralized governance subtract more safety than the aggregation adds. Supply has contracted 3% month-over-month from $1B to $973M, a slow bleed that coincides with the market questioning whether wrapper premiums justify their counterparty overhead. The 89-rated redemption backstop via atomic stablecoin-redeem is U's strongest selling point -- but it also highlights the circular logic of a product whose best exit is unwrapping back into the assets you could have held directly.

reusd-re-protocol.title: Insurance Capital Goes On-Chain
reusd-re-protocol.text: Re Protocol's reUSD channels deposits into a 50/30/20 split of delta-neutral ETH basis trades via sUSDe, short-duration T-bills, and a USDC instant-redemption buffer -- a structure that reads like a reinsurance float deployed across DeFi yield sources. Trading at $1.072 as a NAV-appreciating token, the B- grade at 66 reflects exotic collateral quality and Ethena dependency, while 8.2% APY via Pendle and a 0.24 yield-to-risk ratio position it competitively in the yield-bearing stablecoin field. Supply has surged 38% month-over-month to $177M across six chains, with $18M effective DEX TVL providing genuine secondary-market depth. The queue-based redemption with 20% immediate capacity and BVI FSC licensing won't satisfy institutional compliance teams, but the Chainlink/Network Firm real-time attestation layer and the genuinely uncorrelated reinsurance revenue stream make reUSD one of the more intellectually honest yield products on the market.

rwausdi-multipli.title: The RWA Middleware Layer
rwausdi-multipli.text: Multipli's rwaUSDi wraps 100+ tokenized treasury products, gold tokens, and market-neutral fund units into a single mintable stablecoin — 50% in tokenized T-bills (BUIDL, USDY, OUSG), 25% in aggregated treasury-backed stablecoins, 15% in tokenized gold, and 10% in institutional fund units from Nomura, Fasanara, and Edge Capital. The pitch is that lending protocols can't individually underwrite hundreds of RWA tokens, so rwaUSDi does the aggregation and due diligence — backed by a Lloyd's insurance policy covering de-pegging risk, which is a genuinely novel backstop for a stablecoin. UAE-domiciled with AFI-audited on-chain reserves, it operates on Ethereum only with KYB-gated institutional minting, making it less a retail product and more a composable RWA building block. The elegant abstraction adds a trust layer between holder and underlying assets, but with 99 peg score and only two depeg events on record, the machinery has functioned as designed.

pusd-pleasing.title: Frozen in Place
pusd-pleasing.text: Pleasing USD's supply has been perfectly flat at $120M for at least a month -- identical week-over-week and month-over-month figures suggest minting and redemption have effectively ceased. The Hong Kong precious metals firm's 90% USDT wrapper with 10% tokenized gold exposure sits at a C safety grade of 58, with DEWS having cooled to CALM at 13 from its former Alert-band reading, though 16 depeg events including a 653-bps downside deviation remain on the record. Deployed on Arbitrum and ApeChain with a single DEX pool holding $215K in effective liquidity, the exit infrastructure is barely functional for a coin this size. The issuer-API redemption with multi-day settlement is the only realistic path to par, which makes PUSD less a stablecoin and more a semi-liquid claim on Pleasing International's willingness to honor withdrawals.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaETH's USDm flips the L2 business model: instead of extracting sequencer fees from users, it uses reserve yield from Ethena's USDtb (90% of backing, itself holding BlackRock's BUIDL) to subsidize network operations — the chain literally gets cheaper as more people hold its native stablecoin. A perfect peg score and only two depeg events with DEWS at 2 suggest the product is functioning cleanly, though the absence of any tracked DEX liquidity means exit routes are limited to the redemption mechanism. The dependency on Ethena's infrastructure for both reserve management and custody adds counterparty risk that the underlying Treasury bills don't carry, and the stablecoin's value proposition is inseparable from MegaETH's own traction as an L2. The economics reveal a flywheel where stablecoin adoption subsidizes network costs which drives adoption — elegant when it works, but the flywheel spins in both directions.

usat-tether.title: Tether Goes Domestic
usat-tether.text: Tether's USA-T has nearly doubled from $28M to $50M in two months, backed 80% by T-bills and 20% cash through Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC federal charter with Cantor Fitzgerald custody -- the cleanest regulatory setup Tether has ever assembled. The B report card at 72 with CALM stress at 5 and zero depeg events reflects a product that hasn't had time to accumulate blemishes, though the Ethereum-only deployment and 20 DEX pools with $8.7M TVL suggest distribution is advancing faster than the old summary's liquidity score of 9 implied. The strategic logic is transparent: USA-T is Tether's answer to USDC on US soil, separating the domestic compliance story from USDT's $140B offshore empire. Whether American institutions will trust a Tether-branded dollar after a decade of skepticism is the billion-dollar question -- the early growth trajectory suggests at least some of them will.

yzusd-yuzu.title: Yield Vault in Stable Clothing
yzusd-yuzu.text: Yuzu's yzUSD packages curated DeFi yield strategies into an overcollateralized stablecoin — 50% Pendle PT/LP positions, 20% Euler/Morpho lending, 20% other DeFi strategies, and a 10% USDT0 buffer — all classified as exotic collateral on an unproven chain (Plasma). A perfect peg score and zero depeg events sound reassuring until you note the absence of any DEX liquidity and queue-based redemptions scoring just 56 on the backstop, with the yzPP junior tranche absorbing first losses. The strict KYC gating — only accredited, qualified, or institutional investors can mint and redeem — makes yzUSD one of the most access-restricted stablecoins in DeFi, which explains both the zero depeg events (few holders means few sellers) and the non-existent secondary market. It's a yield aggregator that happens to maintain a dollar peg rather than a stablecoin that happens to generate yield — the distinction matters when things go wrong.

nusd-neutrl.title: The Contraction Test
nusd-neutrl.text: Neutrl's NUSD is being stress-tested by something more revealing than a depeg event: a 24% supply contraction in a single month, from $225M to $170M, as holders queue for the exit. The delta-neutral synthetic dollar backed by 93.5% stablecoins with OTC and hedged positions has maintained composure through the drawdown -- just 4 depeg events total and a CALM DEWS reading of 10 -- which says more about the mechanism than any bull-market AUM figure could. The B- safety grade at 69 with an 8.7% APY via sNUSD yields a modest 0.25 yield-to-risk ratio, respectable for a product with whitelisted queue-based redemption and real-time Accountable attestations. Whether the outflow represents profit-taking or loss of confidence will become clear in the next quarter, but the infrastructure is handling the drawdown with the quiet competence of a product that was built for exactly this scenario.

usdgo-osl.title: The Quiet Surge
usdgo-osl.text: USDGO has more than doubled in supply over the past month to $134 million, a growth rate that makes most stablecoin launches look lethargic, all while maintaining a near-perfect peg with zero depeg events. The safety grade has climbed to B at 71, reflecting 80% T-bills and 20% cash held at Anchorage Digital under an OCC federal bank charter -- credentials that outclass most competitors five times its size. Solana-only deployment and a modest $1 million in DEX TVL across just two pools make this an issuer-API exit story rather than an on-chain arbitrage play, but the CALM stress band and same-day settlement suggest OSL's institutional pipeline is doing the heavy lifting. The real question is whether USDGO's trajectory is sustainable demand from the Asia-Pacific trade corridor or a one-time institutional onboarding that plateaus once the initial wave settles.

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Trillion-Dollar Entrance
fidd-fidelity.text: When the third-largest asset manager on earth issues a stablecoin, the signal overwhelms the product — and the product is deliberately boring: 80% T-bills and 20% cash at BNY Mellon, OCC national trust charter, and a B+ safety grade. At $48M circulating, FIDD is a rounding error on Fidelity's $5.8 trillion AUM, which is precisely the point — this is a regulatory beachhead, not a market play. The 65-rated offchain redemption backstop with same-day settlement is institutional-standard but unremarkable. Four DEX pools with primary coverage and a 66 liquidity score suggest Fidelity is building the on-chain plumbing methodically rather than chasing TVL. The question is not whether FIDD can maintain its peg but whether Fidelity decides this experiment deserves real distribution.

aid-gaib.title: GPU Yield, Dollarized
aid-gaib.text: GAIB's AID is a conventional dollar stablecoin — T-bills and stablecoin reserves, 1:1 mint and burn — whose entire reason for existing is its companion token sAID, which accrues yield from GPU and AI infrastructure financing deals. The structure neatly separates stable value (AID) from exotic yield (sAID), letting users choose their risk exposure. At $21 million market cap it's early-stage even by RWA standards, betting that AI compute demand will create a durable yield substrate. Whether GPU financing agreements produce reliable enough cash flows to back a yield product is genuinely untested — but in a market where every new stablecoin needs a narrative, "AI infrastructure yield" is at least more substantive than most.

apxusd-apyx.title: Dividends as Collateral
apxusd-apyx.text: Apyx introduced what might be the most creative collateral backing in stablecoins: preferred shares from Digital Asset Treasury companies — publicly traded equity from firms like Strategy that hold large crypto positions. The theory is that variable-rate preferred shares trade near par regardless of crypto price volatility, providing stable collateral for a dollar token. Launched on Ethereum in February 2026 with DeFi Development Corp as an early investor, apxUSD is so new that market cap data barely exists. The Protocol-Owned Liquidity buffer is meant to absorb stress, but the underlying question is whether equity dividends from crypto-holding companies are truly uncorrelated with the crypto market they depend on.

jpyc-jpyc.title: The Yen's Licensed Pioneer
jpyc-jpyc.text: Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin occupies an enviable regulatory position — Type II Funds Transfer license under the Payment Services Act, 100% backed by JPY deposits and Japanese government bonds, with institutional-regulated custody and zero transaction fees. Deployed on three chains with the JPYC EX platform handling mint/redemption via bank transfer after KYC, the infrastructure is sound but the market cap remains modest — a product that proves regulatory compliance alone doesn't drive adoption. The real threat isn't GYEN (regulated in New York but locked out of Japan's domestic market) but Progmat Coin from Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui, and Mizuho — three megabanks whose combined balance sheet makes JPYC look like a rounding error. Being first to market matters less when the second movers have trillion-dollar balance sheets and existing banking relationships with every corporation in Japan.

xaut-tether.title: Tether Mints Bullion
xaut-tether.text: Tether's gold token is backed 100% by LBMA Good Delivery bars in Swiss vaults with BDO Italia attestations, operating under El Salvador's CNAD jurisdiction with institutional-regulated custody — the same transparency framework as USDT, applied to physical bullion. XAUT commands the largest share of the tokenized gold market, which sounds impressive until you notice that share has been eroding as PAXG and newer competitors chip away at the margins. Deployed on Ethereum only, XAUT works exactly like you'd expect from Tether: a market that trades on brand recognition over the granular bar-level transparency that Paxos offers with PAXG's allocated serial numbers. With gold's rally inflating all boats, XAUT's real significance may be Tether's own physical gold accumulation rather than the tokenized wrapper itself.

paxg-paxos.title: Fort Knox With a Charter
paxg-paxos.text: The only federally regulated gold token in existence, PAXG operates under Paxos's OCC national trust charter with institutional-top custody, KPMG monthly attestations, and individually allocated LBMA Good Delivery bars at Brink's London — each with a serial number verifiable on the Paxos platform. The permanent second to Tether Gold by market share, PAXG is the first choice for anyone whose compliance department has veto power: allocated bars, bankruptcy-remote trust structure, and the kind of regulatory paper trail that makes institutional allocators comfortable. While XAUT trades on Tether's brand recognition, PAXG trades on verifiable custody — in a market where gold itself is the product, trust infrastructure is the only real differentiator. Ethereum-only deployment limits DeFi composability but matches the product's institutional focus.

kau-kinesis.title: Gold That Pays Rent
kau-kinesis.text: Kinesis cracked the code that other gold tokens missed: people want yield. KAU holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees, paid monthly in additional gold — backed 1:1 by LBMA-approved physical gold at 1 gram per token in ABX vaults, Bureau Veritas audited, under a Cayman CIMA VASP license. Add a virtual Mastercard for point-of-sale gold spending and you get something genuinely different: gold that functions as money, not just an asset, with institutional-regulated custody and independent attestation that the bars actually exist. The catch is that yield depends entirely on Kinesis's transaction volume — if trading dries up, so does the rent check, and without any tracked on-chain contracts, KAU exists primarily within Kinesis's own platform rather than the broader DeFi ecosystem. A growing challenger to the XAUT-PAXG duopoly, betting that yield and spendability matter more than Ethereum composability.

xaum-matrixdock.title: Asia's Institutional Bullion
xaum-matrixdock.text: Matrixdock's XAUm is backed by LBMA-certified 99.99% gold bars at Brink's and Malca-Amit in Singapore and Hong Kong, Bureau Veritas audited, with institutional-regulated custody and a minimum redemption of 32.148 XAUm (1 kg) restricted to KYC'd accredited investors. The Asia-Pacific custody thesis — Singapore and Hong Kong vaults rather than London or Switzerland — is a deliberate choice targeting institutions that prefer regional domicile for their gold exposure. Deployed on Ethereum and BSC, XAUm remains a modest share of the tokenized gold market, but the partnership with Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City for sovereign gold tokenization signals ambitions beyond retail. Whether institutions actually prefer Asia-domiciled custody over the London and Swiss vaults that XAUT and PAXG offer remains the strategic bet.

cgo-comtech.title: DMCC-Stamped Bullion
cgo-comtech.text: ComTech Gold's CGO is backed 1:1 by 24-karat 999.9% physical gold at 1 gram per token in Transguard vaults under the Emirates Group umbrella, DMCC endorsed, with individually serialized bars registered on DMCC Tradeflow and institutional-regulated custody under DAFZA jurisdiction. The redemption-via-app workflow with minimum 10-gram delivery is the most retail-friendly physical gold offramp in the tokenized gold market, leveraging Dubai's regulatory clarity on tokenized commodities that is genuinely ahead of most jurisdictions. Without tracked on-chain contracts, CGO exists primarily within the ComTech ecosystem rather than DeFi, and none of the UAE pedigree has translated into meaningful global adoption. Impeccable local credentials, negligible global presence — proving once again that regulatory clarity alone doesn't create liquidity.

dgld-gold-token-sa.title: Heritage Gold, Rebooted
dgld-gold-token-sa.text: DGLD is backed 1:1 by allocated LBMA Good Delivery PAMP gold bars — the Swiss refiner whose name is synonymous with premium bullion — at 1 troy ounce per token with real-time reserve verification through on-chain bar serial numbers and VQF/FINMA regulatory oversight. MKS PAMP relaunched DGLD in late 2025 with deployments on Ethereum and Base, institutional-regulated custody, and minimum 1-gram redemption — the lowest physical gold redemption threshold of any tokenized gold product. A 60-year refining heritage and the most prestigious gold backing in crypto have produced one of the least adopted gold tokens on the market, proving that heritage is necessary but wildly insufficient for winning the tokenized gold race. The dual-chain deployment signals ambition beyond the institutional market, but DGLD's traction remains a fraction of what PAMP's reputation would suggest.

kag-kinesis.title: The Lonely Ounce
kag-kinesis.text: KAG is backed 1:1 by investment-grade physical silver at 1 troy ounce per token, Bureau Veritas audited under a Cayman CIMA VASP license — the same yield-sharing model as its gold sibling KAU, where holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees paid monthly in additional silver. In a world where tokenized gold has surged past $6 billion, tokenized silver remains a ghost town and KAG is effectively its only resident. Deployed on Ethereum with institutional-regulated custody, the product is structurally identical to KAU but without the macro tailwind: silver's performance has lagged gold's rally dramatically, limiting both demand and yield generation. The thesis is straightforward — if precious metals tokenization is real, silver must eventually follow gold — but 'eventually' is doing a lot of heavy lifting for a product this niche.

eurq-quantoz.title: The Enterprise Euro
eurq-quantoz.text: Quantoz built EURQ for corporate treasurers, not DeFi degens — DNB-regulated under MiCA, 102% reserved in 68% eurozone government bonds and 32% cash at Tier 1 European banks, with direct SEPA integration and institutional-regulated custody. The same Dutch compliance infrastructure as its USDQ sibling, EURQ carves a niche in programmable corporate payments where compliance is a feature, not a tax. The 2% over-collateralization buffer and self-reported transparency are a quiet flex: enough to signal conservatism without dragging capital efficiency, supervised by the same DNB that oversees ING and ABN AMRO. Whether the enterprise market actually wants an on-chain euro or just talks about it at conferences remains the open question, but Quantoz is better positioned than most to find out.

deuro-deuro.title: The Oracle-Free Euro
deuro-deuro.text: Born from the same codebase as Frankencoin (ZCHF), dEURO takes the contrarian position that price oracles are a point of failure, not a feature — its CDP model uses internal auctions instead of external price feeds, a design that trades capital efficiency for resilience against oracle manipulation. The collateral is omnivorous: 40% WBTC, 25% WETH, 10% XAUT (tokenized gold), and smaller positions in USDC, DAI, UNI, and ZCHF, all valued through auction-based mechanisms on five chains. With governance fully transferred to token holders and no founder control over contracts, dEURO is genuinely decentralized in a euro stablecoin market where that word usually means 'we have a multisig' — one of only two decentralized euro stablecoins tracked by Pharos. MiCA's evolving stance on decentralized stablecoins could be either tailwind or existential threat, depending on whether European regulators view oracle-free design as innovation or evasion.

cetes-etherfuse.title: Three Counterparties, One Yield
cetes-etherfuse.text: CETES are Mexico's equivalent of Treasury bills — zero-coupon sovereign debt auctioned weekly by the Ministry of Finance — and Etherfuse has tokenized them into a NAV-accreting instrument backed 100% by CETES with INDEVAL custody, institutional-regulated oversight under CNBV/IPAB/CONDUSEF, and independent attestation. The BBB- sovereign rating is honest about where Mexico sits in the credit hierarchy — legitimate investment grade, but peso volatility means dollar-denominated exposure carries FX risk that doesn't appear in the APY headline. Deployed across four chains (Solana, Base, Polygon, Stellar), CETES tokens offer genuine access to Mexican sovereign debt for holders who can navigate the KYC-gated minting process. The yield is real and Banxico's rate cycle has kept CETES competitive globally — what the token hasn't resolved is which of its three dependencies (the peso, the sovereign, or the issuer) will cause the first inconvenient conversation.

zarp-zarp.title: The Rand's Digital Outpost
zarp-zarp.text: ZARP is backed 100% by ZAR in a treasury managed by Old Mutual Wealth — one of Africa's largest financial institutions — independently audited by Kempen, with institutional-regulated custody and an FSCA CASP license still pending. Deployed across Ethereum, Base, and Polygon, the infrastructure is sound but adoption has plateaued despite genuine demand for stable local-currency rails in a country where the rand regularly loses ground to the dollar. South African crypto regulation remains in perpetual draft mode, and ZARP's problem isn't credibility — it's relevance in a market that hasn't yet decided whether local-currency stablecoins solve a problem or just add complexity to existing USD pairs. For the small audience that needs on-chain ZAR exposure, ZARP is the only regulated option; for everyone else, USDC denominated in dollars remains simpler.

syrupusdc-maple.title: Institutional Lending, Vaulted
syrupusdc-maple.text: Maple Finance's syrupUSDC has become one of the largest yield-bearing stablecoins, channeling deposits into overcollateralized institutional loans. The ERC-4626 vault design makes it composable enough that Aave V3, Morpho, and Pendle have all integrated it — meaning your lending yield can itself be lent, borrowed against, or split into principal and yield tranches. Base expansion saw deposit caps fill immediately, suggesting institutional credit appetite exceeds available supply. The risk is the one that always haunts institutional credit: borrowers default, and 'overcollateralized' is only as good as the collateral's liquidation value in a downturn.

syrupusdt-maple.title: The Mirror Vault
syrupusdt-maple.text: Maple's USDT counterpart to syrupUSDC runs on identical mechanics — ERC-4626 vault, institutional borrower pool, overcollateralized credit lines — as the smaller sibling. The distinction matters less than it appears: both feed from the same Maple lending infrastructure, and yield differentials between the two are negligible. Ethereum-only deployment limits its DeFi composability compared to syrupUSDC's multi-chain reach, which may explain the size gap. For yield-seekers who prefer their stablecoin exposure in Tether rather than Circle, syrupUSDT is the vault; the economics are otherwise indistinguishable.

yousd-yield-optimizer.title: Fifty Strategies, One Token
yousd-yield-optimizer.text: YO Protocol's yoUSD automates what DeFi power users do manually — rebalancing USDC across 50+ yield sources on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Unichain, ranked by risk scores with per-pool and per-protocol concentration caps. The track record of positive returns with zero negative months looks miraculous until you remember it was built during a bull market. Backed by Paradigm, Haun Ventures, and Coinbase Ventures, the deposits are modest but growing as the NAV appreciation model means your 'dollar' climbs steadily above $1 — stable in the sense that it never goes down, not that it stays at one. The real tension is philosophical: yoUSD is a sophisticated yield aggregator wearing a stablecoin's clothing, and the distinction matters when the bull market ends.

ustb-superstate.title: Wall Street's On-Chain Fund
ustb-superstate.text: Superstate's USTB sits at $810 million in 100% short-duration government securities at BNY Mellon, sub-advised by Federated Hermes, audited by Ernst & Young -- a pedigree that reads like a traditional fund prospectus because it essentially is one. The B+ safety grade at 75 with A+ in resilience and dependency risk makes it one of the highest-rated yield-bearing tokens on Pharos, though the SEC Reg D restriction to qualified purchasers and accredited investors means the audience is narrow by design. Zero DEX liquidity and zero pool count confirm that USTB doesn't trade on decentralized markets at all; this is a subscribe-and-redeem product at daily NAV, now at $11.05 per share yielding 3.20%. The real significance remains infrastructural: USTB appears in the collateral stacks of other stablecoins that want Treasury exposure without the BNY Mellon relationship, making Superstate less a consumer product than the institutional plumbing beneath DeFi's yield layer.

ousg-ondo-finance.title: The Hundred-Dollar Stablecoin
ousg-ondo-finance.text: OUSG has grown past $700 million — 85% backed by BlackRock's BUIDL with 12% in BlackRock's FedFund and a 3% USDC liquidity buffer, making Ondo I LP BlackRock's largest single on-chain client and OUSG essentially a first-class derivative of BlackRock's tokenized money market presence. At over $114 per token with NAV appreciating daily, it is the least dollar-like entry on any stablecoin dashboard, which is why Ondo maintains rOUSG — a rebasing sibling that stays at $1 while OUSG accumulates. The SEC investigation closure in November 2025 without charges removed the key regulatory overhang, and the instant T+0 mint/redemption via OUSGInstantManager against USDC through BUIDL on-chain liquidity makes OUSG's exit infrastructure better than most tokenized funds. Restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers with on-chain KYC enforcement — tokens literally cannot transfer to non-whitelisted addresses — OUSG is less a stablecoin and more a tokenized mutual fund that borrowed the infrastructure.

mtbill-midas.title: Europe's T-Bill Token
mtbill-midas.text: mTBILL is Midas's compliance-first answer to the tokenized T-bill race: 97% in BlackRock's IB01 ETF with Swiss custody at Maerki Baumann, issued as a Liechtenstein FMA-approved MiFID II instrument — the exact bureaucratic architecture required to legally sell T-bill exposure to European professionals. Ankura Trust provides daily on-chain NAV attestations, and the RWA collateral quality with regulated-entity governance earns institutional credibility that most crypto-native tokenized treasury products lack. The 'not available to U.S. or UK retail persons' restriction is the mirror image of USTB and OUSG's American access gates, carving out a European institutional niche in a market dominated by U.S. issuers. Deployed across five chains, mTBILL functions as infrastructure in Midas's product stack and as stable collateral in third-party structured products — the European T-bill token for protocols that need regulatory certainty over DeFi composability.

wsrusd-reservoir.title: Ashes to APY
wsrusd-reservoir.text: Reservoir's rUSD processed $285M in redemptions 'without failure' in November 2025, then flatlined — the protocol's precise way of surviving a bank run while losing the patient. The reincarnation as wsrUSD is an ERC-4626 NAV vault backed by an unusually varied diet: 30% USDC, 25% USDT, 10% PYUSD, 5% GHO, 5% RLUSD, 5% USD1, plus strategy vaults and lending markets — seven upstream stablecoin dependencies curated by Steakhouse, Gauntlet, and other named managers. Credit Enforcer smart contracts enforce minimum 105% liquidity, solvency, and capital ratios before any leverage-increasing action, which is the kind of on-chain risk management that most yield protocols skip. Deployed across 15 chains with exotic collateral quality and multisig governance, wsrUSD's flexibility is genuine — but the seven-dependency architecture means the protocol's safety is a derivative of Circle, Tether, PayPal, Aave, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial simultaneously.

dusd-alto.title: The Isolated Vault Stablecoin
dusd-alto.text: Alto DUSD takes a kitchen-sink approach to collateral in isolated markets — 55% ETH and LSTs, 20% BTC tokens, 15% sUSDe, 5% Syrup USDC, and a 5M USDC PSM cap at 20 bps — so one bad collateral doesn't cascade into the rest. The 91-rated PSM backstop with permissionless atomic settlement is the structural highlight, and the perfect peg score with zero depeg events on $527K in circulation suggests the architecture works at micro-cap scale. DAO governance via ALTO token holders earns the decentralized classification, though the DEWS Watch band at 29 with 85% worst-pool stress signals that the on-chain market is thinner than the collateral diversity implies. The embedded Ethena dependency via sUSDe means DUSD inherits a slice of delta-neutral basis risk on top of its overcollateralization buffer — sophisticated risk engineering at a scale too small to stress-test.

dusd-dtrinity.title: Post-Exploit Purgatory
dusd-dtrinity.text: The March 17 exploit hit dTRINITY at the worst possible moment — a protocol with genuinely novel economics (subsidized borrowing funded by reserve yield) now carries a danger notice that overshadows everything else on the page. Supply has contracted to roughly $1.5M from $1.8M a month prior, Sonic deployment is paused, and the C grade at 57 reflects a protocol where the safety floor has cracked. The reserve composition tells the dependency story: 42% sfrxUSD and 35% Curve AMO positions mean dUSD is overwhelmingly a bet on Frax infrastructure, with chain-isolated reserves that at least prevent cross-chain contagion. DEWS has eased from Alert to Watch at 20, suggesting the acute crisis is stabilizing, but the 84-rated backstop with 40% immediate capacity is doing the heavy lifting to keep this from unwinding further. An elegant flywheel that proved fragile under pressure — the borrower subsidy model deserves a second chance, but this protocol needs to earn it.

thbill-theo.title: Wrapping the Wrappers
thbill-theo.text: Theo's thBILL is 100% backed by tULTRA, which wraps Standard Chartered Libeara's ULTRA fund, which holds actual U.S. T-bills managed by Wellington Management — three entities and two wrappers between your token and a government bond. The Panama-incorporated structure with single-entity governance and no published proof of reserves contrasts sharply with the Ankura-attested mTBILL and E&Y-audited USTB it competes against, though Standard Chartered's custody and Wellington's management provide institutional ballast at the bottom of the stack. The RWA collateral quality and institutional-regulated custody classification acknowledge what's actually holding the assets, even if the wrapper depth adds layers of operational risk that the T-bill label might obscure. Deployed across four chains with KYC-gated minting and T+4 settlement on underlying collateral, thBILL has found its niche among institutional investors who want T-bill exposure without caring too much about how many wrappers sit between them and the bonds.

usdp-parallel.title: Fee Yield, No Tricks
usdp-parallel.text: Parallel's USDp is backed 50% by sfrxUSD and 50% by sUSDe — two yield-bearing stablecoins whose Parallelizer module adjusts minting and redemption fees dynamically to correct peg drift without oracles or liquidation cascades. The yield story is unusually honest: sUSDp distributes 70% of actual protocol fees from the Parallelizer, bridging, and flash loan modules, meaning yield tracks real usage rather than governance votes on a made-up rate. DAO governance across five chains with Bailsec audit and Certora formal verification suggest Mimo Labs built this for durability rather than speed, though the dependency on both Frax (sfrxUSD) and Ethena (sUSDe) means USDp inherits the risk profiles of two very different stablecoin architectures — one backed by BlackRock T-bills, the other by delta-neutral basis trades. The central tension is whether a fee-revenue yield model can remain attractive at small scale when it competes against synthetic dollar protocols running leveraged strategies at hundred-fold the size.

usdpt-western-union.title: Remittance Giant Meets Federal Charter
usdpt-western-union.text: Western Union moves $200B+ in cross-border remittances annually and has decided the next leg of that journey runs through Solana. USDPT is issued by Anchorage Digital Bank — the first federally chartered OCC crypto bank — with reserves custodied at U.S. Bank and Western Union providing the distribution network spanning 200+ countries and half a million retail locations. The March 2026 media blitz tells the real story: CEO McGranahan went on Fox Business to explain the business model — converting Western Union's 'negative float' (paying partners to hold funds) into positive float revenue from treasury assets. Crossmint now handles wallet infrastructure, Rain is building a stablecoin-linked Visa prepaid card targeting inflationary markets, and the company wants to onboard community banks currently stuck on SWIFT. CoinGecko already has a preview listing with zero supply, which means the infrastructure is assembled but the token isn't circulating yet. The 170-year-old money transfer company may not need to compete for DeFi liquidity — its physical footprint is the moat.

roughrider-bnd.title: State-Owned Banking Goes On-Chain
roughrider-bnd.text: North Dakota's Bank of North Dakota — the only state-owned bank in the US — cleared its biggest hurdle on March 25 when the Industrial Commission unanimously approved the bank-to-bank use case for Roughrider Coin. Ten local banks have already expressed pilot interest, CEO Don Morgan rates the risk as 'low to moderate,' and the project is expected to be cost-neutral to the state. The coin runs on Solana via Fiserv's infrastructure, backed by USD reserves and 93-day Treasury notes under the GENIUS Act's state-issued stablecoin exemption. It won't be publicly tradeable — this is pure interbank settlement plumbing, voluntary for ND banks and credit unions. September 2026 remains the target, pending Fiserv contract finalization. As the second US state stablecoin after Wyoming's FRNT, Roughrider represents an emerging pattern: state treasurers discovering that blockchain settlement is cheaper than correspondent banking, even when the vote requires a closed-door executive session lasting two and a half hours.

fiusd-fiserv.title: The Payments Stack Play
fiusd-fiserv.text: Fiserv processes $2 trillion in payments annually for 6,000+ financial institutions and wants to make stablecoins just another rail in that plumbing. FIUSD is less a single stablecoin and more a platform: Paxos handles issuance, Circle provides ecosystem interop, PayPal enables interoperability, and Mastercard connects the payments network. The centralized-dependent classification captures this architecture accurately — FIUSD depends on an entire constellation of partners, any of which could become a bottleneck. The end-of-2025 launch target has quietly slipped into 2026 with no firm date, which either means careful regulatory preparation or the inherent difficulty of coordinating four major fintech companies on a shared timeline.

eur-qivalis.title: Twelve Banks, One Euro
eur-qivalis.text: Qivalis is the European banking establishment's answer to USDC and Tether: a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin backed by a consortium of 12 major banks including BNP Paribas, ING, UniCredit, and BBVA. The reserve design — 30-40% bank deposits, the remainder in short-term eurozone government bonds — reads like a money market fund with a blockchain address. The blockchain question is now settled: Ethereum mainnet first (ERC-20), then Polygon and Base, all with a permissioned KYC layer — only pre-verified participants can hold or transfer the token, which is the banking consortium's compromise between public chain liquidity and institutional control. CEO Jan-Oliver Sell (ex-Coinbase Germany) is finalizing exchange partnerships, with Bit2Me named as one platform in discussions. The EMI license application has been filed with De Nederlandsche Bank but not yet granted. The central tension remains whether twelve banks that compete fiercely in every other market can cooperate long enough to ship before Circle's EURC and SocGen's EURCV eat the entire MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin market.

pusd-polaris.title: Immutable CDP, Yield Included
pusd-polaris.text: Polaris Finance is building what its co-founders TokenBrice and 0xLuude call the successor to Liquity's ethos: a crypto-collateralized stablecoin on Ethereum with immutable core contracts, no admin keys, and no off-chain assets. pUSD is minted against pETH collateral via CDPs, and the yield-bearing angle comes from protocol revenue — borrowing interest, swap fees, conversion gains, and DEX fees — rather than from depositing reserves into Aave. The private testnet is live with a Q4 2026 target, which gives the team time to prove that you can ship immutability without sacrificing usability. For a market saturated with centralized fiat-backed tokens and yield products built on leverage, pUSD is a deliberate bet that there's still demand for the Liquity V1 philosophy, upgraded.

pgold-polaris.title: Synthetic Gold, No Vault Required
pgold-polaris.text: Polaris Gold shares infrastructure with its sibling pUSD but pegs to gold rather than the dollar — and critically, does so without any physical gold backing. Unlike XAUT or PAXG, which tokenize actual bars in Swiss vaults, pGOLD is a synthetic gold exposure minted from the same pETH collateral pool via CDPs on Ethereum. This makes it arguably more decentralized than any gold-pegged token on the market, at the cost of carrying all the risks of crypto collateral in a down market. Whether DeFi users want synthetic gold exposure from immutable contracts instead of custodied metal from Tether or Paxos is an experiment Polaris is willing to run.

usg-tangent.title: Productive Collateral, Dynamic Rates
usg-tangent.text: Tangent Finance — which pivoted from the Convergence protocol after an August 2024 exploit — is building USG as an over-collateralized CDP stablecoin that accepts productive DeFi collateral: Curve LP tokens, Pendle PTs, and Stake DAO positions rather than raw ETH or stablecoins. The peg mechanism borrows from crvUSD’s playbook: dynamic interest rates and a rewards deduction rate automatically increase when USG drifts below $1, incentivizing borrowers to repay. A yield-bearing sUSG vault (ERC-4626, built on Yearn v3) lets holders capture 25% of protocol earnings passively. Four audits are complete — Sherlock (Sep 2025), Egis, and two Pashov reviews (Oct-Dec 2025) — and the protocol has moved from auditing into beta testing, with mainnet deployment still ahead. The design bets that DeFi-native collateral can be more capital-efficient than traditional CDP models, though it inherits the composability risk of every protocol whose tokens it accepts.

klarnausd-klarna.title: Buy Now, Settle On-Chain Later
klarnausd-klarna.text: Klarna — the Swedish fintech with 114 million customers and $112B in annual GMV — is building a stablecoin via Stripe's Bridge infrastructure on the Tempo L1. Tempo mainnet went live on March 18 with sub-second finality, fees under $0.001, and a Machine Payments Protocol co-authored with Stripe for autonomous AI agent payments — yet KlarnaUSD was conspicuously absent from the mainnet launch partners list (which included Anthropic, Mastercard, Visa, and Revolut). Bridge's conditional OCC national bank trust charter, approved in February, strengthens the regulatory foundation for KlarnaUSD issuance. The coin remains on Tempo's testnet for now, making it a matter of 'when' rather than 'if.' The interesting dynamic hasn't changed: Klarna doesn't need external adoption for KlarnaUSD to succeed — its own payment volume is large enough to justify the infrastructure, making DeFi liquidity a bonus rather than a requirement.

trusd-tori.title: Ethena's Mirror, Three Days Old
trusd-tori.text: Tori Finance soft-launched trUSD on Ethereum on March 24 with the same playbook Ethena popularized: a synthetic dollar backed by delta-neutral trading positions (futures arbitrage, calendar spreads, hedged money markets) with a yield-bearing staked wrapper (strUSD, ~15% APY advertised). Delphi Ventures led the seed round alongside QInvest, CMCC Global, and Bering Waters. Accountable provides real-time proof of reserves via its DVN, and two audits are complete (Sherlock Jan 2026, Nethermind Mar 2026). The bull case writes itself — institutional yield strategies democratized at $1 minimums. The bear case is equally obvious: contract addresses are still listed as 'TBA' in the docs, the app endpoint refused connections during our research, TVL shows N/A on their own site, and the Nethermind audit was completed the same day as the 'launch.' Not on DefiLlama, not on CoinGecko, 17 total tweets. This is a controlled beta marketed as a mainnet launch, and the 0.1% mint/redeem fee plus 10% performance fee structure means Tori needs meaningful AUM before the economics work. Watch for contract publication and aggregator listings before treating this as anything more than a proof of concept.

ussd-sonic-labs.title: Yield Without the Yield
ussd-sonic-labs.text: USSD is Sonic Labs' answer to why a fast EVM chain should depend on Circle and Tether to denominate everything — a permissionless, zero-fee stablecoin backed entirely by tokenized T-bills (BlackRock BUIDL, Superstate USTB, WisdomTree WTGXX) and built on Frax's frxUSD smart contract infrastructure. The design choice that distinguishes it from every other T-bill-backed stablecoin is also its most pointed: the Treasury yield flows to the Sonic ecosystem as buybacks and incentives, not to USSD holders, meaning every dollar sitting in USSD generates a return that benefits the protocol's treasury while the holder earns exactly $1. At roughly $2M in circulation at launch, this subsidy is trivial; at meaningful scale, it becomes a permanent off-balance-sheet revenue stream funded by users who chose the zero-yield option. The GENIUS Act-compatible framing and U.S. jurisdiction signal suggest Sonic Labs is building for a regulatory environment that hasn't fully arrived yet, which will look prescient or premature depending entirely on how fast Washington moves.

pgold-pleasing.title: Gold Without Receipts
pgold-pleasing.text: Pleasing Gold's PGOLD is backed 1:1 by LBMA-standard 99.99% physical gold at 1 troy ounce per token, deployed on Arbitrum and ApeChain — the same Pleasing International that issues PUSD, sharing infrastructure and the Hong Kong precious metals firm's physical gold corridor. The institutional-unregulated custody and absence of any proof of reserves or independent attestation make PGOLD the least transparent gold token on the dashboard, relying entirely on the issuer's claims without external verification. Whether a gold token without audited reserves can compete with PAXG's KPMG attestations and XAUT's BDO Italia audits depends on the holder's trust in the issuer rather than the metal itself. For Pleasing's existing gold corridor clients, PGOLD may serve as a convenient tokenized bridge; for everyone else, the lack of verifiable custody is a hard pass.

ggbr-goldfish-gold.title: The Paper Gold Token
ggbr-goldfish-gold.text: Goldfish Gold's GGBR represents 1/1000 of a troy ounce of gold per token, but unlike XAUT or PAXG, the backing is described as 'issuer balance-sheet gold exposure' rather than allocated physical bars — making it more a gold-tracking derivative than a tokenized commodity. The institutional-unregulated custody with no published proof of reserves, no independent attestation, and no disclosed jurisdiction means the entire trust chain runs through the Goldfish entity alone. Ethereum-only deployment with high-risk reserve classification reflects the Pharos assessment of what 'issuer-managed backing' means in practice: counterparty risk on the issuer rather than custody risk on the metal.
