In a tokenized gold market where PAXG offers individually serialized LBMA bars with KPMG attestations, GGBR's value proposition is hard to articulate beyond convenience.

axcnh-anchorx.title: The Offshore Yuan
axcnh-anchorx.text: AnchorX's AxCNH is a CNH-pegged stablecoin backed 100% by offshore Chinese yuan cash reserves at regulated financial institutions, issued under a Kazakhstan AFSA license — a jurisdiction that provides formal regulatory cover without the scrutiny of Hong Kong or Singapore. The institutional-unregulated custody classification and absence of proof of reserves or independent attestation mean the trust assumptions sit entirely with the AnchorX entity and its reported reserve figures. Deployed on two chains, AxCNH occupies an unusual niche: on-chain access to CNH exposure for a currency whose on-shore variant (CNY) is heavily capital-controlled by the People's Bank of China. Whether the offshore yuan stablecoin market is large enough to sustain a product without established exchange partnerships or DeFi integrations remains the open question.

idrt-rupiah-token.title: Indonesia's Digital Rupiah
idrt-rupiah-token.text: Rupiah Token's IDRT is backed 100% by Indonesian rupiah bank deposits held by PT Rupiah Token Indonesia, deployed natively across four chains — making it one of the more broadly distributed local-currency stablecoins despite operating with institutional-unregulated custody and no published proof of reserves. Indonesia's crypto market is among the largest in Southeast Asia, giving IDRT a genuine addressable market for IDR-denominated on-chain transactions and remittances, though the absence of specific regulatory licensing and independent reserve attestation limits the product to users who trust the issuer directly. The domestic regulatory landscape for stablecoins in Indonesia remains in development, meaning IDRT operates in a gray area where compliance is self-defined rather than externally enforced. For a country with genuine demand for affordable digital payment rails, IDRT's existence is more practical than innovative.

tryb-bilira.title: The Lira's Digital Outpost
tryb-bilira.text: BiLira's TRYB is a Turkish lira stablecoin backed 100% by TRY cash reserves, deployed natively across seven chains — the broadest distribution of any local-currency stablecoin in the Middle East and North Africa region. The institutional-unregulated custody and absence of proof of reserves or specific regulatory licensing reflect the current state of Turkish crypto regulation, where stablecoin issuance operates without a formal licensing framework. Turkey's double-digit inflation and persistent lira weakness create genuine demand for digital TRY rails — the same macro dynamics that make PikuDAO's USP profitable as a carry trade make TRYB useful as an on-ramp for Turkish crypto traders who need local-currency denomination. Seven-chain deployment suggests BiLira is building for breadth rather than depth, covering the chains where Turkish users actually trade.

ebusd-ebisu.title: Gold and Shorts on Plasma
ebusd-ebisu.text: Ebisu's ebUSD is a Liquity V2-style CDP with one of the most eclectic collateral baskets on the dashboard: 44% sUSDe (Ethena's yield-bearing token), 24% WBTC, 24% XAUt0 (Tether Gold on Plasma), 6% stcUSD, and 3% weETH — mixing synthetic dollars, wrapped Bitcoin, tokenized gold, and ETH LSTs into a single overcollateralized position. At barely $260K in market cap with 169 depeg events and persistent below-peg trading, ebUSD is too small to attract meaningful arbitrage, and the 78-rated collateral redemption backstop provides a structural floor that the thin secondary market can't close efficiently. Deployed natively on both Ethereum and Plasma with user-set interest rates, the Liquity V2 architecture is sound but the alt-LST-bridged collateral quality classification and DEWS Watch band at 35 reflect the risk profile of accepting tokenized gold and basis-trade derivatives as CDP backing. ebUSD is a micro-cap experiment in exotic collateral CDP design — interesting architecture on a scale too small to stress-test.

usdaf-asymmetry.title: Decentralization's Price Tag
usdaf-asymmetry.text: USDaf achieves what almost no stablecoin can claim: immutable contracts and a perfect governance score, built on Liquity V2 with collateral drawn from the yield-bearing stablecoin canon -- 65% ysyBOLD, 23% scrvUSD, 7% sUSDS, and scraps of tBTC, sfrxUSD, and WBTC. The B- safety grade at 66 is a significant upgrade from the C it held last month, though the price of recursive decentralization remains steep: $1.04M in circulation (down 33% from last month), 103 depeg events, and a current price of $0.986 that suggests the Liquity V2 redemption floor around $0.995 isn't always reached in practice. The 82-rated permissionless collateral redemption backstop is structurally sound, and six DEX pools provide more coverage than a million-dollar stablecoin typically deserves. USDaf is the purest expression of trustless stablecoin design currently live -- and also a reminder that the market values liquidity over ideology.

usnd-nerite.title: Immutable Code, Invisible Scale
usnd-nerite.text: Nerite's USND earns an A safety grade at 83 on $1.3 million in circulation -- the highest safety score you'll find at this market cap, built on immutable Liquity V2 contracts on Arbitrum with permissionless collateral redemption. The collateral is 86.5% tBTC with rETH and WETH rounding out the reserve, giving it A+ marks in both decentralization and dependency risk that most nine-figure stablecoins can't match. But the DEWS Watch band at 19, 172 depeg events, and a worst deviation of 1,016 basis points positive reveal the cost of being small: the peg wobbles because there's nobody on the other side of the trade. DEX liquidity is $14K across three fallback-class pools, meaning the backstop's 82-rated permissionless redemption is the only real exit. USND is the answer to a question very few people are asking yet -- whether you can build a truly decentralized, immutable stablecoin that scores well on every metric except the one that requires other people to care.

ftusd-flying-tulip.title: Cronje's Carry Trade
ftusd-flying-tulip.text: Andre Cronje's Flying Tulip raised $225 million to build a DeFi super-app, and the stablecoin at its center has attracted roughly $730K in circulation from 20 holders — a ratio of venture capital to actual usage that would make a Web2 startup blush. The delta-neutral pitch echoes Ethena's playbook but runs a domesticated version: USDC and USDT lent into Aave with borrowed native assets staked to generate carry, no CEX perpetuals in sight. Yield flows exclusively to sftUSD stakers while unstaked ftUSD proceeds feed the protocol treasury, a design that makes the base token a zero-yield stablecoin whose holders subsidize the protocol by default. Deployed on Ethereum and Sonic with single-entity governance, circuit breaker contracts, and full dependency on the two largest centralized stablecoins, ftUSD is less a standalone dollar and more an opt-in yield wrapper for USDC and USDT with extra steps.

brla-brla-digital.title: Brazil's Dollar Problem, Inverted
brla-brla-digital.text: Most stablecoins let emerging-market users escape their local currency into dollars. BRLA does the opposite: it tokenizes the Brazilian Real for on-chain use, backed by government bonds (titulos publicos) and BRL cash held by Avenia (formerly BRLA Digital), a Sao Paulo startup with $17M in Series A funding. Deployed natively on Polygon, Gnosis, Celo, and Moonbeam with no Ethereum presence, BRLA's chain footprint is unusual — Celo dominates with 76% of the ~$14.7M supply. The contract is upgradeable with full blacklisting via a COMPLIANCE_ROLE, governed by a single entity with no multisig or DAO, and proof-of-reserves attestations are self-reported on a Notion page. Yield variants (stBRLA, yBRLA) exist as separate tokens, positioning BRLA as infrastructure for BRL-denominated DeFi rather than just a remittance rail — though at sub-$15M market cap, the infrastructure is still looking for its builders.

silk-shade-protocol.title: The GDP-Weighted Privacy Dollar
silk-shade-protocol.text: SILK is what happens when you cross a stablecoin with a macro index fund and deploy it on a privacy chain. Pegged to a GDP-weighted basket of 20 global currencies — USD at 30%, CNY at 22%, EUR bloc at 14%, plus JPY, GBP, INR, and fourteen others — SILK doesn't track any single fiat currency, making it one of the most conceptually ambitious stablecoins tracked on Pharos. Built entirely on Secret Network using the SNIP-20 privacy token standard, every transaction is private by default with optional auditability via viewing keys. The stability architecture layers overcollateralized lending (ShadeLend), stablecoin redemption pools, bounded minting with DAO governance, and ShadeDAO bonds — a belt-and-suspenders approach deployed on a chain that most DeFi users have never touched. At ~$1.1M in circulation on a single unproven chain with no bridge to Ethereum, SILK is simultaneously the most interesting basket stablecoin in crypto and one of the hardest to actually acquire.

idrx-idrx.title: Eighteen Billion Tokens, One Dollar
idrx-idrx.text: IDRX is PT IDRX Indo Inovasi's fiat-backed Indonesian rupiah stablecoin, deployed natively across eight chains with built-in bridge functions and CertiK-audited contracts -- architecturally more ambitious than its rival IDRT, even if the market doesn't seem to care yet. At roughly $1.1M in circulating supply denominated in a currency where each token is worth $0.000058, the token count runs into the billions while the economic value barely registers. The B- safety grade at 65 is surprisingly strong for a token with no published proof of reserves, no named custodian, and explicit blacklisting capabilities baked into the contract. DEWS sits at a calm 9 across $252K in DEX liquidity spread thinly over nine pools, which is technically diversified but practically illiquid. Supply has been quietly trickling down month-over-month, suggesting organic contraction rather than growth -- the Indonesian crypto market may ultimately decide it needs zero rupiah stablecoins rather than two.

mxnb-juno.title: Bitso's Quiet Peso Play
mxnb-juno.text: MXNB is the Mexican peso stablecoin from Juno, a product of Bitso — Latin America's largest crypto exchange — operated through a licensed IFPE (electronic payment funds institution) called NVIO PAGOS MEXICO. The contract architecture tells the whole story: it's a FiatTokenV2_2, the exact same Centre/Circle codebase that powers USDC, complete with blacklisting, pausing, and upgradeability. Deployed at the same address across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Avalanche with quarterly attestation reports following International Valuation Standards, MXNB is a textbook regulated fiat stablecoin — just denominated in pesos instead of dollars. The transparency page reports reserves exceeding circulating supply at ~20.8M MXN, though with only 117 holders on Ethereum and a $1.1M USD market cap, the token's reach is currently closer to a pilot program than a payment network. Listed on Kraken and a handful of DEXes, MXNB is infrastructure waiting for a use case — or perhaps the use case waiting for Mexican DeFi to find it.

cjpy-yamato.title: ETH-Backed Yen, Quietly Running
cjpy-yamato.text: Yamato Protocol's CJPY is a JPY-pegged stablecoin built on a clean, ETH-only CDP model by DeFiGeek Community Japan — a DAO with no corporate entity behind it. The mechanism echoes Liquity's playbook: deposit ETH at 130% minimum collateralization, borrow CJPY with a one-time fee and no accruing interest, and face liquidation via a subrogation system that uses accumulated protocol fees to automatically repay underwater positions. The redemption floor — 1 CJPY always redeemable for 1 JPY worth of ETH from the riskiest pledge — provides a hard price floor without forced liquidation penalties. Deployed only on Ethereum with ~$1M in circulation, CJPY occupies the same philosophical space as RAI and LUSD: minimal governance, pure crypto collateral, no blacklisting, no upgradeability theater. The YMT governance token with veYMT vote-escrowed mechanics is planned but the protocol currently runs with DAO oversight via Snapshot. In a market where JPY stablecoins are dominated by centralized issuers like JPYC and GYEN, CJPY is the decentralized alternative that almost nobody uses — which, for its builders, may be precisely the point.

usdkg-gold-dollar.title: Kyrgyz Gold, Dollar Wrapper
usdkg-gold-dollar.text: USDKG is a sovereign experiment in commodity-backed stablecoin design: the Kyrgyz Republic's Ministry of Finance sold 376 kilograms of LBMA Good Delivery gold bars to LLC Virelint Group, which stores them in sealed boxes at an unnamed bank, and the state-owned OJSC "Issuer of Virtual Assets" mints USD-pegged tokens against that pile. The gold is real — Kyrgyzaltyn, the state mining monopoly that refined it, has been LBMA-listed since 2022 — but the trust chain from bullion to token runs through private intermediaries whose bank won't even let auditors see the access logs. Kreston Global's quarterly report is an ISRS 4400 agreed-upon procedures engagement, not an audit, and it explicitly disclaims assurance — a distinction that matters when 100.6% overcollateralization is the only buffer between a gold price dip and undercollateralization. The ConsenSys Diligence smart contract audit found no critical issues but confirmed what the architecture implies: owner multisig can pause all transfers, compliance multisig can blacklist any address and destroy its tokens. At $50M across Tron and Ethereum with thin DEX-only liquidity, USDKG is less a stablecoin for DeFi and more a cross-border payments rail for Central Asian corridors — the question is whether Bishkek's gold vaults can inspire the same confidence as, say, Brink's London.

usdh-hermetica.title: Bitcoin's Synthetic Dollar, On Stacks
usdh-hermetica.text: Hermetica brings the Ethena playbook to Bitcoin-native infrastructure: BTC spot plus short perpetual futures creating a delta-neutral synthetic dollar, deployed exclusively on Stacks L2 with a Runes variant on Bitcoin L1. At $9 million in circulation from a protocol that raised $1.7 million in seed funding, USDh is the smallest delta-neutral stablecoin on the dashboard and the only one that touches neither Ethereum nor a single EVM chain. Yield flows to sUSDh stakers via funding rate payments from the short perpetual positions, with Hermetica advertising up to 25% APY — a figure that depends entirely on perpetual funding rates staying positive, which historically they do until they catastrophically don't. Minting requires KYC/AML verification through Hermetica's app, collateral sits on centralized exchanges, and a DIA oracle prices the token on-chain — a trust stack that makes this less a trustless Bitcoin dollar and more a managed fund with a Clarity smart contract wrapper. The single-chain, single-entity design is refreshingly honest about what it is: a bet that Bitcoin's basis trade can sustain a stablecoin ecosystem outside the EVM monoculture.

usdsc-startale.title: Sony's Dollar, M0's Plumbing
usdsc-startale.text: USDSC is what happens when a Sony-backed L2, a Singapore web3 studio, and M0's T-bill infrastructure converge on the thesis that every blockchain needs its own branded dollar. The token is a 1:1 wrapper around M — the same short-term Treasury bill reserves, the same on-chain Validator attestations, the same bankruptcy-remote SPV structure — repackaged with freeze authority and a Soneium-exclusive deployment for Startale's app ecosystem. At $4 million in supply on a single chain with 6,000 holders, USDSC is less a stablecoin competing for market share and more a distribution play: onramp through MoonPay, transact in the Startale App, earn yield through sUSDSC vaults audited by Quantstamp, OpenZeppelin, and four other firms. The bet is that Sony's Soneium — an OP Stack L2 with 500 million transactions — generates enough user gravity to make a chain-native stablecoin viable where dozens of others have failed. Whether the world needs another M0 wrapper with a different logo remains an open question, but the institutional lineage is harder to dismiss than most sub-$5M coins can claim.

ctusd-citrea.title: Bitcoin's Dollar, MoonPay's Rails
ctusd-citrea.text: ctUSD is the native stablecoin for Citrea, the first Bitcoin ZK-rollup, issued by MoonPay and powered by M0's T-bill infrastructure — the same bankruptcy-remote SPVs, the same on-chain Validator attestations, the same short-term Treasury backing that now underwrites half a dozen branded dollars across the ecosystem. At roughly $1 million in circulation on a single chain that most DeFi users have never heard of, ctUSD's value proposition is less about the dollar and more about the distribution: MoonPay's 30 million verified users can buy in via Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal across 49 U.S. states and 160+ countries, making the on-ramp wider than the destination chain's current user base. The Founders Fund and Galaxy Digital backing lends the kind of institutional credibility that typically accompanies products ten times this size, while Citrea's Bitcoin-secured ZK-rollup architecture means ctUSD settles on the most decentralized base layer in existence — even if the stablecoin itself is as centralized as every other M0 derivative. The bet is straightforward: Bitcoin needs a native, compliant dollar to unlock DeFi beyond wrapped-BTC vaults, and MoonPay's fiat rails plus M0's reserve plumbing make ctUSD the path of least resistance for that thesis.

usdat-saturn.title: Saylor's Yield, M0's Backing
usdat-saturn.text: Saturn pitches itself as the digital monetary layer for a financial system backed by Bitcoin, but at launch USDat is just another M0 wrapper — 100% of the collateral is short-term Treasury bills via M0 Protocol, which means the dollar in your wallet is bankrupt-remote SPV plumbing wearing Saturn's logo. The Bitcoin part lives one floor up, in the sUSDat staking vault, where capital is dynamically rotated into STRC — Strategy's perpetual preferred equity — based on Michael Saylor's loan-to-value ratio, targeting 11%+ APY routed through Clear Street custody and a Securitize-administered BVI fund. USDat is permissioned and geofenced from the United States, the EEA, and OFAC jurisdictions, so the audience is sophisticated offshore capital comfortable with both KYC onboarding and a 3-7 day unstaking queue. With $33 million in circulation barely a month after the March 2026 deployment, three audits from Certora and Three Sigma, and live proof-of-reserves still pending Accountable and Chainlink integration, USDat is the cleanest expression yet of the thesis that crypto's next yield wave doesn't come from on-chain perps or RWA T-bills — it comes from being long whatever Saylor is short.

usdk-orki.title: Swellchain's Restaked Dollar
usdk-orki.text: Orki Finance brings Liquity V2's immutable CDP architecture to Swellchain, accepting LST and LRT collateral like swETH and rswETH to mint USDK — a design that bets the entire protocol on the restaking thesis staying solvent. At roughly $10K in circulation, USDK is less a functioning stablecoin and more a proof of concept that Liquity's code can be deployed wherever restaked ETH derivatives accumulate. The collateral mix of liquid staking and liquid restaking tokens earns an alt-lst-bridged-or-mixed quality classification, reflecting the layered smart contract risk inherent in assets that are themselves wrappers of wrappers. User-set interest rates and permissionless collateral redemption with Liquity-style dynamic fees preserve the decentralized governance story — no admin keys, no multisig, no entity to call when things go sideways. Whether Swellchain generates enough DeFi activity to justify a native overcollateralized dollar remains the open question, but at least the architecture is honest about what it is: a minimalist borrowing primitive for restaking degens who want leverage without leaving the chain.

usdq-quill.title: Scroll's Liquity Outpost
usdq-quill.text: Quill Finance deploys Liquity V2's immutable CDP blueprint on Scroll, minting USDQ against wETH, wstETH, weETH, and — notably — SCR, Scroll's own native token, which injects a layer of alt-L1 governance token risk that Liquity's Ethereum-native design never contemplated. At roughly $132K in circulation, USDQ is a micro-cap stablecoin on a Stage 0 zk-rollup, meaning both the dollar and the chain it lives on are still proving themselves. The collateral mix earns an alt-lst-bridged-or-mixed classification: LST derivatives are reasonable CDP fodder, but accepting SCR as collateral ties the stablecoin's health to the market sentiment of the very chain hosting it — a reflexivity loop that gets uncomfortable in a drawdown. Immutable code and Liquity-style dynamic redemption fees preserve the decentralization credentials, with no admin keys or multisig to intervene when collateral ratios tighten. The thesis is that Scroll needs a native overcollateralized dollar and Liquity's battle-tested architecture is the safest way to build one — but with supply this thin, the real test is whether anyone shows up to use it.

chfau-allunity.title: The Frankfurt-Zurich Pipeline
chfau-allunity.text: AllUnity's CHFAU extends the Deutsche Boerse consortium's stablecoin ambitions from the euro to the Swiss franc, backed by the same DWS-Galaxy-Flow Traders alliance that produced EURAU and regulated under the same BaFin EMI license. CHF reserves sit 1:1 at CRR credit institutions in segregated accounts, a reserve model that is aggressively boring by design — MiCA's EMT rules prohibit interest on token holdings, so CHFAU competes on trust infrastructure rather than yield. At roughly 2.5 million CHF in early circulation on Ethereum alone, it enters a CHF stablecoin market shared with VNX's VCHF and Frankencoin's decentralized ZCHF — three philosophically distinct approaches to putting the Swiss franc on-chain. The safe-haven currency angle is real: in periods of macro stress, CHF demand spikes, and having a MiCA-compliant on-ramp with institutional-grade plumbing positions CHFAU for a use case that only materializes when everything else is going wrong.

buck-buck-assets.title: The Bitcoin Dollar Bet
buck-buck-assets.text: BUCK bills itself as "the world's first SavingsCoin" — a yield-bearing stablecoin whose treasury is 77% Strategy Inc. perpetual preferred stock, making it less a dollar and more a leveraged view on MicroStrategy's Bitcoin conviction with a dollar wrapper. The yield story (targeting 7% annually via STRC dividends, distributed as monthly rebases) is compelling until you trace the dependency chain: STRC pays dividends from a company whose entire thesis is that Bitcoin goes up forever, which is either a feature or a ticking clock depending on your priors. A BVI-domiciled entity with a single-entity governance model, upgradeable proxy contracts, and a denylist — controlled by ex-Uber and ex-Bird executives — is not the typical stablecoin trust model, though monthly attestations from The Network Firm add a layer of professional accountability. At roughly $2 million in circulation with 261 holders and negligible DEX volume, BUCK is currently a micro-cap experiment in whether you can build a savings product on top of someone else's Bitcoin maximalism.

bd-basedollar.title: Liquity's Fork, Aerodrome's Yield
bd-basedollar.text: Base Dollar takes Liquity V2's battle-tested CDP architecture and replants it on Base with a twist: instead of ETH collateral, borrowers deposit LP tokens — routing the stablecoin's security model through Aerodrome's liquidity layer and harvesting AERO farming rewards as the yield engine. Revenue splits three ways between users, a protocol-owned liquidity treasury, and BD stakers, a design that ties the protocol's survival to the depth of Base's DEX ecosystem rather than ETH price alone. The project recently completed an external audit that surfaced a high-severity LP token price manipulation vulnerability and a medium-severity timelock bypass, both now remediated with fuzz testing added — the kind of findings that are routine for a Liquity fork adapting to exotic collateral types but worth watching post-launch. Still in the auditing phase with a Q2 2026 target, Base Dollar is betting that LP-collateralized debt positions can offer better capital efficiency than vanilla ETH CDPs, though the trade-off is inheriting every smart contract risk in the Aerodrome stack on top of its own.

wm-m0.title: The Plumbing's Plumbing
wm-m0.text: wM is the non-rebasing wrapper that turns M0's yield-bearing T-bill token into something a normal ERC-20 contract can hold without breaking — and the price of that convenience is that holders volunteer to forfeit the yield. Underneath sits the same 30-to-90-day Treasury bills, the same bankruptcy-remote SPVs, the same Validator attestations as M itself, but the WrappedMToken contract routes all accrued yield to TTG-approved earner accounts (read: the downstream M0 ecosystem — USDat, USDSC, ctUSD, mUSD, USD0, and friends) via claimExcess(), leaving wM holders with a flat dollar that does nothing. There is no blacklist, no freeze, no pause function — a refreshingly minimal surface for a centralized stablecoin — and wrap/unwrap are open and free, so the peg holds by pure arbitrage against M. At roughly $93M in circulation across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Plume, and Solana, wM is the composability primitive the entire M0 ecosystem builds on top of: nobody is meant to hold it directly, everyone is meant to hold something built from it. It is the cleanest expression of M0's thesis that the yield should belong to whoever bothers to put the dollar to work, not to whoever happens to be holding it when the music stops.

usdnr-nerona.title: A Private Bank for Five Wallets
usdnr-nerona.text: Nerona USD is a $50M M0-wrapper stablecoin issued by a private-wealth-management startup that has so far convinced exactly five wallets to hold it — a holder count more befitting a family office than a stablecoin. The token is structurally a thin wrapper over M0's $M (collateralised by Superstate's USTB Treasury fund and minted by MXON), and despite Nerona's marketing copy promising capital that 'works while you don't', USDnr itself is non-yield-bearing: the T-bill carry accrues to the M0 reserve and Nerona, not to holders. Governance is single-entity, redemption is permissioned and KYC-gated, and the wrapper inherits every M0-layer risk — minter insolvency, M0 governance deactivation, and the small matter of being unregulated. Mind the symbol: this is USDnr (Nerona, on Ethereum), not USDN (Noble's M0-wrapper on Cosmos) — sloppy press copy and screenshots conflate the two, but they share nothing beyond the M0 plumbing underneath. A private bank for the onchain era, with a circulating-supply-to-holders ratio that rounds to $10M per client.

usdk-kast.title: The Anjouan Card Dollar
usdk-kast.text: KAST Dollar is what you get when a Comoros-domiciled fintech wraps M0's tokenized T-bills, slaps a card on top, and quietly pockets the yield. The token sits on Solana as a Token-2022 mint with permissioned transfer hooks and confidential-transfer extensions wired in — useful if you trust KAST and BitGo, awkward otherwise. At roughly $24M outstanding it is still proof-of-concept scale, riding entirely on M0 Validator attestations rather than its own audit trail. Holders earn nothing; if you want the T-bill carry you're nudged into USDKy, KAST's separately rebasing twin. The legal stack — KAST Tech in Anjouan, custody by partners, 'not a bank' disclaimer in bold — is the modern offshore neobank uniform. A cleaner version of buying T-bills than most card-app stablecoins, provided you've made peace with single-jurisdiction issuer risk and a regulator most maps don't bother to label.

xo-exodus.title: Self-Custody's Custodial Dollar
xo-exodus.text: When a self-custody wallet best known for letting users hold their own keys decides to mint its own dollar, the result is XO Cash: a MoonPay-issued, M0-wrapped Treasury claim wearing an Exodus hoodie. The reserves sit in MoonPay's regulated SPVs and the M0 yield quietly accrues to the issuers, not the holders, which is the polite way of saying XO is a payment rail with a stablecoin garnish. Token-2022 ships with pausable, transfer-hook, and permanent-delegate authorities all held by a single MoonPay key, so the 'self-custody' marketing applies to your wallet but not to your tokens. Initial proof of product-market fit was paying X Games athletes $2,500 signing bonuses, which is either a charming retail use case or a launch metric in search of a thesis. Backed by short-dated Treasuries, geofenced where it has to be, and aimed squarely at the Exodus Pay card audience that has never asked what an SPV is.

rgbp-revolut.title: 13 Million Users, One Brand Ban Away
rgbp-revolut.text: Revolut got its full UK banking licence on March 11 after a 20-month mobilisation — and promptly confirmed its proposed GBP stablecoin would NOT be issued from the new banking entity. Bank of England rules prohibit a UK bank and its affiliated group from issuing stablecoins across different subsidiaries, so issuance falls back to Revolut Ltd, the e-money entity. That structural wrinkle is the smaller of Revolut's UK regulatory headaches. At the House of Lords on March 25, Head of UK Policy Rory Tanner told peers the UK is 'already behind' the US and EU — and flagged the BoE's proposed ban on 'branded' stablecoins as a commercial blocker (the issuer couldn't put its own name on the token). Priority use case per Tanner: the UK→India remittance corridor, the seventh-largest in the world, not retail payments. The FCA sandbox cohort Revolut joined on Feb 25 is testing phase only; the full UK authorisation regime doesn't activate until October 2027, and the BoE's proposed 40% unremunerated-reserve requirement plus £20,000 individual-holder cap describe a commercial model that UK legal analysts call structurally unviable. Revolut's real asset isn't the token — it's 13 million UK users who already open the app daily. Whether that distribution survives the BoE rulebook is the actual question.

ausdt-tether-alloy.title: Gold Collateral, Dollar Target
ausdt-tether-alloy.text: Alloy Tether turns Tether Gold into a dollar-tracking credit instrument: verified users deposit XAUT into an Ethereum vault, mint aUSDT against a 75% mint-to-value ceiling, and return aUSDT plus fees to withdraw collateral. That gives Pharos a clean on-chain reserve view because the XAUT backing sits in the CMPVault, but it also means aUSDT inherits Tether Gold custody, gold-price volatility, whitelist access, and liquidation mechanics. The peg is not a bank-account promise; it is an overcollateralized gold position engineered to trade near one dollar.

usdsui-sui.title: Sui Gets Its Native Dollar
usdsui-sui.text: USDsui is the Sui ecosystem dollar issued through Bridge, Stripe's stablecoin infrastructure arm. The asset gives Sui a native fiat-backed stablecoin rather than another bridged dollar, with DefiLlama exposing supply and price data for live peg monitoring. The reserve model is conventional Bridge Open Issuance: cash, short-dated Treasuries, repos, and government money-market funds support mint and redemption. Pharos tracks the runtime supply and peg through DefiLlama while keeping reserve composition curated until Bridge exposes a USDsui-specific public reserve feed or Sui supply probe suitable for live reserve sync.

brlv-crown.title: Brazilian Bonds On Chain
brlv-crown.text: Crown BRLV is a Brazilian real stablecoin backed by federal government bonds pledged for token holders through a security-agent structure. That is a cleaner reserve story than most emerging-market fiat coins: the backing is local sovereign debt rather than offshore dollar liquidity, and the legal structure is designed to keep reserve claims separate from Crown itself. The risks are equally specific: BRL liquidity, Brazilian sovereign-rate volatility, and KYC-gated redemption. Pharos tracks the BRL peg directly while treating reserves as curated-validated evidence until Crown's reserve page proves machine-readable enough for a dedicated adapter.

usdglo-glo.title: Public-Goods Float
usdglo-glo.text: Glo Dollar is a Brale-issued U.S. dollar stablecoin whose reserve yield funds public-goods causes rather than flowing back to token holders or exchange partners. The mechanics are familiar: cash, cash equivalents, and short-duration U.S. government-backed debt, monthly attestations, and 1:1 mint and redemption through Brale. The differentiation is distribution and mission, not financial engineering. At small supply, USDGLO matters to Pharos because it already appears inside other reserve stacks such as Mento, making explicit tracking useful for dependency analysis even before it becomes a large standalone market.

usdon-ondo.title: Ondo Settlement Cash
usdon-ondo.text: USDon is the dollar settlement token inside Ondo Global Markets, backed 1:1 by U.S. dollars in brokerage accounts and used to move between cash and tokenized assets. It is closer to platform settlement cash than a standalone retail stablecoin, which shapes the risk model: institutional rails, access restrictions, and dependence on Ondo's Global Markets structure. CoinGecko provides the runtime price and market-cap path, while Pharos models reserves as brokerage-account cash and redemption as a whitelisted platform route until Ondo exposes a dedicated public liquidity or reserve feed.

audm-macropod.title: Australia's New On-Chain Dollar
audm-macropod.text: Macropod AUDM brings an Australian-dollar unit into the active Pharos set with DefiLlama supply, CoinGecko pricing, Ethereum and Solana contracts, and issuer documentation describing segregated AUD reserve accounts at Australian ADIs. The product is straightforward: approved Macropod clients can mint and redeem through the platform, with current reserves split mostly between Westpac and Banking Circle Australia. The main constraints are scale and disclosure cadence. Pharos can monitor the AUD peg immediately and validate live token supply, while a monthly-report adapter would be needed for stronger reserve automation.

busd0-usual.title: Fixed-Maturity USD0 Bond
busd0-usual.text: bUSD0 is Usual's fixed-notional USD0 bond, formerly USD0++, with a June 11, 2028 maturity. It is backed by locked USD0 but does not behave like a spot stablecoin before maturity: par exit requires both bUSD0 and the separate rt-bUSD0 early-exit right, while secondary-market bUSD0 can trade below one dollar. Yield is paid through USUAL coupons rather than dollar NAV growth, so the risk is a mix of USD0 reserve quality, Usual DAO parameter risk, and liquidity/discount risk before maturity.

stusds-sky.title: Sky Risk-Capital USDS
stusds-sky.text: stUSDS is Sky's expert-mode risk-capital token, not a plain sUSDS savings receipt. Deposited USDS funds SKY-backed borrowing while idle liquidity earns the Sky Savings Rate, exposing holders to borrower shortfall, governance slashing, utilization, and withdrawal-liquidity risk. It inherits the broad Sky/USDS ecosystem but should rank differently from USDS and sUSDS because its value can be affected by staked-SKY loan performance.

stcusd-cap.title: Cap Yield Wrapper
stcusd-cap.text: stcUSD is the yield-bearing version of Cap cUSD. Users stake cUSD into an ERC-4626 vault while Cap operators borrow reserve assets against restaker collateral and repay with yield above the hurdle rate. Cap's design attempts to keep stablecoin holders whole through overcollateralization and slashing, but stcUSD still adds operator, restaker, strategy, and vault risk on top of the underlying cUSD basket.

said-gaib.title: AI Infrastructure NAV Token
said-gaib.text: sAID is GAIB's staked AID vault token. Unlike AID, which is intended as the stable base currency backed by Treasuries and accepted stablecoins, sAID floats with the NAV of AI infrastructure financing positions plus stable reserve buffers. Monthly withdrawal cycles, unrealized-loss-aware unstaking NAV, and private AI financing exposure make it a materially different asset from AID.

msy-main-street.title: Main Street Strategy Share
msy-main-street.text: msY is Main Street's yield share over msUSD. It accrues value from the protocol's options and derivatives strategy reserve, while final exit ultimately depends on converting back through msUSD and Main Street's USDC redemption process. The token therefore carries strategy execution, exchange/custody, liquidity, and governance risk that should not be folded into the base msUSD row.

yusd-yieldfi.title: YieldFi USDC Strategy Vault
yusd-yieldfi.text: YieldFi yUSD is an ERC-4626 vault over USDC that allocates capital across Pendle principal tokens, Morpho and Silo vaults, and private-credit vaults. Its stability depends on USDC as the native underlying, but its holder risk comes from active allocator decisions and the performance of those yield venues. Pharos tracks it separately from Aegis YUSD and YO Protocol yoUSD because the name collision hides a distinct issuer and reserve strategy.

sbold-k3-capital.title: K3 Stability Pool BOLD
sbold-k3-capital.text: sBOLD is K3 Capital's ERC-4626 wrapper around BOLD deployed into Liquity V2 Stability Pools. It earns interest and liquidation gains while automating the conversion of liquidated ETH and LST collateral back into BOLD. The base BOLD system is immutable and fully on-chain, but sBOLD adds K3-controlled vault, oracle, solver, and fee-switch risk, so it belongs as a separate wrapper exposure.

stkgho-umbrella-aave.title: Aave Umbrella GHO Staking
stkgho-umbrella-aave.text: Aave Umbrella stkGHO is the slashable GHO staking receipt for Aave's upgraded safety module. It is backed by GHO, but unlike liquid GHO or simple savings GHO, holders accept Umbrella-specific cooldowns, withdrawal windows, and automated slashing if covered GHO deficits occur. That makes it a distinct loss-absorption asset rather than a plain yield venue on the base stablecoin.
